The Campaign is a step above the first game, lots of outfits, extras etc. But... at the end of the day, it falls short of being solid. The story is also very good, and wholesome. 

Resident Evil: Revelations 2 takes a more open book approach to its mechanics. If you played Resident Evil 6 and the first Revelations, you'll appreciate things like sprinting, manual dodging, smoother animations, better graphics, more puzzles, etc. But eventually you'll feel like the sum is less than the resources they've pulled from... 

"What the heck is this guy on about?"
Resident Evil 6: A overdone, packed game with mechanics you might not ever use, based in fully functional Co-Op,  lots of relevant multipurpose things to buy with your game currency, a simultaneously running story that doesn't force you to replay the same area again with different characters (It has reason to do this), being ridden with QTEs and more.
Revelations 2 takes the mechanics of the engine, makes the co op one sided where it feels tacked on. (Your partner is basically a item finding flashlight that can save you from grabs and assist in combat, but mostly support bound) Campaign skills are all over the place, and some require getting skills you don't care for to unlock.

Some things are just bad.
Zombies can grab you through walls, making you have to struggle despite being behind a tile wall with a barred bulletproof glass window. Same areas are inaccessible after a tense thing happens. Want to get that chest when your partner isn't in danger anymore? No, now the game won't prompt you to climb up there. The default aim speed is the same speed or slower than a running pig enemy, so if you're shooting them wondering why you can't keep up with it... that's why. 

The AI... makes Palicos, Palamutes, Shakalaka, and etc look like scholars. If you for one second think that you'll just chill and use the secondary character and chill out. No. You need to get a skill for the primary character to care enough to shoot on their own, and despite the partner character healing the player when they need help, the primary character will not heal themselves when AI controlled, and will often get themselves killed when you have thoughts like: "Oh only the secondary character passively heals to full health, I'll just do all the dirty work with them" Here comes your AI controlled sandbag trying to headbutt a two handed blunt weapon wielding zombie... Fantastic idea, let's see how th-... oh, if the primary character dies, even when AI controlled, you can't revive them. 

If you're looking for co op... no. Don't do it to your friend. What I can give this game though, is that it might make for a good experience if someone who already beat it plays support, and the new person plays the primary character, maybe if you've got a child too. I just got to the point where I just remain in a dying state, I swear every time I heal and get touched, I'm back dying anyway so I just save them. 

As for Raid Mode... it's just arena based gauntlets so far. open spaces where you fight enemies as they appear and try your best to not heal and conserve ammo, a lot of them are areas from Resident Evil 6. Why they didn't just put this stuff in that game is far beyond my understanding, as the mechanics might have allowed it more success, especially with dives, rolls, quick shot and etc. Daily quests grant outrageous amounts of experience, and the amount of outfits and customization already beats the first game. But what also kills the experience outside of the mode itself, gun attachments outside of story mode require you to either destroy the attachment to add a different one in the slot, or destroy the entire weapon to get the skills back. And maybe it's just me, but that seriously brings out the Breath of the Wild player in me, where I ruin my experience so I can keep all of my skills and don't suffer losing them or paying to break weapons I'm going to pay to replace later. Late game, if you have or seek rare attachments it's most likely going to suck deciding which weapon gets it, because if you change your mind later, you either have to grind another skill, or trash your weapon.

(Someone pointed out they used emotes from Lost Planet 2, and that gave me so much false hope lol.)

While it's seriously grueling in the first game, the weapon and skill unlocks made me feel like I was given the ability to play the campaign the way I wanted to. And while this campaign is definitely better, you're not going to be able to simulate that freedom. I guess it's not much to worry about nowadays, as Capcom treats Resident Evil like their golden egg, but I sincerely hope they get better at their mechanics, so more happy accidents like Onimusha and Devil May Cry happen, you know?

[h1]A Sad Take On A Loved Franchise[/h1] 
Resident Evil: Revelations 2 is an episodic survival horror video game developed and published by Capcom as part of the Resident Evil series. The game is a follow up to Resident Evil: Revelations and Resident Evil 5. It marks the return of Claire Redfield as the protagonist, and the first time Barry Burton is a playable story character in the main series.

        [td]💾Graphics[/td]
        [td]The graphics are not that bad actually. The UI though, is absolutely messy and terrible. I can not stand the design of it. The environmental detail and design is really top notch and impressive, especially for a game made in 2015. The lighting is not that good though. It’s bland and I never seen the reason for the flashlight (besides to stun the enemy and find “hidden” items). The enemy and boss design is actually really good and enjoyed every enemy in the game in a deisng perspective. They are spooky and give you the creeps. I also do like the character designs here (specifically Barry).[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]🎮Gameplay[/td]
        [td]The gameplay is pretty good in my opinion, but with some issues I don’t like at all. I would say the movement is really good in this one. The gunplay is pretty good and fits with the fast action this game provides. You do have to switch between characters through the game. Claire is your main character, while Moira can flash the enemy with her light. If you switch to her you can light up objects through the map and get extra ammo and medical supplies, same goes for Barry's companion, Natalia, except she can see enemies through walls. You do have a good amount of weapons in this game as well. You also can upgrade your weapons which is really cool. This gives you a more focus on specific weapons of your choosing. The biggest gripe I have is the mouse controls. I get this weird input lag, I can't put my finger on it. Also the camera movement is really weird and brings me a feeling of hate for this game. If you are using a controller, then you will have zero issues at all. Raid mode in this game is an absolute blast! You have a good selection of characters and levels. You can level up your characters and unlock new perks, and upgrades for your weapons. The levels are fast, fun, and can be really challenging. I think it's the best Raid mode out of any RE game out there.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]📜Story[/td]
        [td]The story was pretty average in my opinion. The only part of the story I enjoyed was the whole Barry trying to find his daughter. You have two sides to the story. One is you play as Claire Redfield and on your side you have Berry's daughter Moira Burton, who was captured and taken into an abandoned island and they have to find a way out. On the other side, you play as Barry trying to find his daughter 6 months after their capture. It had some good parts in it, but I can’t see myself enjoying a second playthrough on it. It doesn’t help that you have to buy the rest of the story as DLC’s, which is just comedic. Imagine doing part of the story just to wait next week or so to buy and play another piece then to just wait again. It blows my mind they actually did that.[/td]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]🎭Multiplayer[/td]
        [td]The multiplayer is actually pretty fun. You have a Raid mode you can play with some other players. I actually had a blast with this on my Xbox and it still is fun here with friends. Not much to say about the multiplayer. It’s fun, the levels are fast to go through and can provide a challenge.[/td]
    [/tr]

        [td]🕛Playtime[/td]
        [td]The campaign took me over 11 hours to beat. There are two endings I believe (I'm currently on my 2nd playthrough) so you do have some replayability, especially with easy achievements here (from what I saw). The Raid Mode will provide some extra time especially with a friend.[/td]
    [/tr]

Besides that, the sound effects are pretty good actually and the guns sound really nice. Also the enemies sounds scary which is a plus.[/td]

First of all Revelations 1 and Revelations 2 are not really connected to each other. They play and feel like 2 different games. 
The story is divided into 4 episodes and each episode is either played with Moira and Claire in the past scenario or with Barry and Natalia in the present scenario. 
Claire and Moira (daughter of Barry) work for a biohazard prevention agency. While they attend an office party, they get captured by armed soldiers and are taken to a facility on an island. In the first episode they try to escape (past scenario) while in episode 2 (Barry and Natalia) try to find them both in the present scenario and that's how the episodes are split up,
It's a Survival Horror game and you are playing every character in third person. The controls were smooth and you can always switch between the two characters in each episode. Playing with my AI teammate was done well, too. The graphics are fine and I personally liked the atmosphere in this game a lot. The weapons felt powerful and you find a lot of inspirations of Franz Kafka. Whether you were playing against enemies or bosses, I never felt my teammate was useless or annoying. 
I personally enjoyed playing this game and I do recommend playing it, since it has a well written story and the atmosphere is catching. You better check the material and I personally do not regret playing it!

What an amazing game. It is so, SO MUCH better than Revelations 1 in every possible way.

The fluid combat of 4/5 - each shot meaningful, staggering/disabling/stunning with accuracy - have returned and although it's not retained a few positive mechanical improvements of 6 (e.g. diving, sliding, quick-shot), it's restored CQC to not be excessive at detriment of the overall experience. Revelations 2 continues the Resident Evil storyline with camp dialogue and an b-movie plot, nothing bombastic or pretentious as either 5 or 6, and although it doesn't have the grace of Code Veronica, it certainly has an equal appeal as a scenario: a desolate island hosting subjects to experience their worst fears in the machinations of a bioweapon fare.

Environment design is an improvement to the drab nature of 5 or the insipid details of 6, exploring a mine which isn't chainlinked tunnels and a wooded area that has enemies as unpredictable in their location through the disorientation of dense treelines. The fundamental underground laboratory has returned, a monolith of a tower that's foreboding on the island, radio towers as hope, a self-destruct timer as a classic feature and a memorable cliffside battle - all setpieces to combine for a distinct Resident Evil experience which is not limited to dull plateau or repetitively undescript corridors.

Main characters are designed well - principal negative being a little derivative from TLOU's bland style - and their animations are smooth. Additionally, mobility of movement has reintroduced the tactical element of 4/5, positioning, and subsequent movement, integral for any battle - moving whilst shooting weak in pace for this to be less negative for this factor - whilst a new dodge function - substituting either diving or invincibility from item pick-ups - embellishes the intensity of gameplay: powerfully tactical, worryingly precise and scarily intense.

Monster bosses are fantastic, notably Neil Fisher's 'metamorphosis' and the final boss, as ever - animations responsive to attacks, move sets reasonable (forgiving a few instant death moments which are not fair/balanced) and health/damage balanced. They're aesthetically intriguing and each have backstories to not be hollow. Furthermore, bosses - designed to look creepy as they are fearsome - are interesting as ever, movement and shots requiring a certain tactical acumen which create a tense situation.

The flaws (i.e. interface and characters mainly):

1 - Blind & Dying alignment - unbalanced and an annoyance. It is a frustration - incapable of clear visuals momentarily - and when combined with the cumbersome changes to the health system for recovery, it's increasingly an annoyance along with being a frustrating experience.

2 - Bottles, Bottles, Bottles. Cloth, disinfectant, alcohol. The processes are repetitive and the crafting is distracting for the experience to lose a certain flow. Where are grenades which were beautiful for AOE damage aesthetically and also logical in appearance/availability/applications (e.g. incendiary, flash, explosive)? Grenade launchers - staple of Resident Evil? What is with the clutter of different health items for a myriad of states? Complexity is not inherently positive.

3 - Vapid characters with the exception of Neil Fisher and the main cast (but Barry's daughter). Their costumes are dull and their mannerisms are worse - they have nothing distinctive as Raymond in Revelations as one instance. A few are unlocked in Raid Mode and it's unlikely for anyone to be play them whilst they have neither charisma to personality/actions or individuality in appearance - fundamentally flawed as 'choices' which are (literally) pedestrian.

4 - Poor weapon customization and weak ability modifiers. The ability/weapon enhancements are superfluous overall, sometimes magical to have the characters as riduculous, and are not addictive/personalised as 4/5; customization or character differences seldom significant and occasionally absurd, cheap innate differentials for power in health or damage with Y as examples. The system in Raid Mode is overly open, too, and specialization is less prominent for each character to have them each feel less unique in their traits or advantages.

Incidentally, Raid Mode returns and it is absolutely great - progressively difficult and varied: a primary feature of Revelations 2 which should persuade anyone to purchase it. The combat is demonstrated as flawless - blind state withstanding along with dubious specializaion- and the content is immense.

Co-op campaign is nice as a compromise from both characters being strong and the secondary character having a speciality - lacking any weapons - which does balance well: establishing a fun, interactive dynamic for teamwork with ascertaining enemy vulnerabilities, distracting the enemy, blinding them and locating items.

Finally: HUNTERS! HUNK! These are excellent and I am excited for further enemies/weapons/costumes in DLC to broaden the experience to Outbreak's level.

[h1]Disclaimer[/h1]
I played through first episode on Survival, episodes 2-3 on Normal.

[h1]TL;DR[/h1]
If you liked RE4, but wanted less consistency with mechanics then this will be your jam.
While RE4, 5 and 6 embraced their action genre, this game has some design choices that seem to try putting it more towards survival-horror, but since it still focuses on combat a lot – you end up with a game that’s neither a full survival-horror nor a horror shooter.

I can only recommend for RE fans who want to play all the games in the series. Revelations 2 is probably one of the worst ones.

[h1]Description[/h1]
In RE Revelations 2 you will play as 2 pairs – Clair + Moira (Barry’s daughter) and Barry + Natalia (a small girl and a new character). This game has nothing to do with Revelations 1, there is no need to know both for full story.

This game has the ability to move and shoot at the same time, unlike RE4. It’s also a solo game where you will switch between 2 characters in real time, even during combat.

While in Resident Evil 5, 6 and Revelations 1 every pair had both characters being able to shoot, move objects etc. in Revelations 2 each character contributes in different ways.

Claire and Barry can shoot and have CQC training that lets them knock down stunned enemies. Moira can stun enemies with her flashlight and finish them off when they are on the ground, but can’t knock them down. She can also use her light to look for hidden items. She cannot use guns however. Natalia can sense zombies even through walls, detect weakpoints on enemies and throw bricks to knock them down. She can also sneak around better than other characters and can uncover hidden items like Moira.

Also, Barry, as an elite operative, is fully equipped for combat from the get-go, unlike other protagonists.

The story follows Claire and Moira after their kidnapping by unknown group of soldiers. They end up in cells of a prison with zombies walking around and they have to find a way out. Barry on the other hand follows their trail in order to find his daughter.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
[b]+ Atmosphere[/b]
The game is pretty oppressive (not as much as RE3 or Evil Within) and visual design keeps the tension on. Zombies tend to be very old and decomposed.

[b]+ Combat (when AI isn’t dumb)[/b]
I liked RE5’s combat for it’s integration of tag-team melee combos. Here you can have similar teamwork, but you have to switch between characters. You can blind an enemy with a flashlight as Moira, then knock him down with a kick as Claire and finish off with Moira again.
Natalia can throw a brick at an enemy, which will knock them down and possibly reveal a weakpoint for Barry to shoot for a quick kill. While Natalia cannot do as much damage as Moira by herself – Barry is more than enough to kill anything in their path with her ability to detect enemies and weakpoints.

[b]+ Raid[/b]
A game mode where you go through premade dungeons fighting enemies and collecting items and money to upgrade your character. Can be played in co-op. This is the best part of the game.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
[b]- Stealth[/b]
Unless a game is build around it (like Evil Within 2) stealth has no place in horror games (or games in general). Here stealth does not work half the time, probably due to full on scripting of some enemies.

[b]- Episodic[/b]
I’m pretty sure I got this game in a bundle with other RE games and there was nothing in the bundle that told me that I would only get 1 Episode out of 4. Imagine my disappointment when I finally sit down to play this after reserving a good portion of a weekend for gaming and finding out I need to shill some more money down Capcom’s way for the pleasure of not ruining my weekend.

If all episodes are out, then why the f is the game still being sold piecemeal...

[b]- Searching mechanics[/b]
There are 2 search mechanics in this game. For Claire and Moira, the latter handles the flashlight and if she shines light at a spot with a hidden item – a small sparkling effect will appear. Then you have to manually take over Moira and aim her flashlight at the hidden item spot, which will then reveal the item for you to pick up.
For the other duo, the girl will detect nearby item spots just by looking in their direction. She then has to point at them by aiming, which will reveal the item for both her and Barry.

This is an annoying mechanic that just makes you double-check every corner of every room. Items should just be there for you to find and pick up without these special mechanics.

It’s still a better system than the awkward scanning from Revelations 1. God, I’m glad that got scrapped.

[b]- Difficulty/AI[/b]
I started playing on Hardcore, but at some point the game expects you to use melee attacks a whole lot because you won’t have enough ammo for some bosses. Problem is, unlike in RE 4/5, you can’t just shoot an enemy in the head to put them in a stun state. Stun is achieved either randomly when you hit an enemy with a gun, or by focusing with your flashlight for a few seconds. While you are controlling one character who uses flashlight, the other one will very often wander into enemy range and get mashed into the ground. You can tell your partner to stay somewhere safe, but only Claire can knock enemies down with a kick once they are stunned. Moira can attack in melee and finish opponents on the ground, but doesn’t receive a prompt to kick. So you are either grinding away at enemies using Moira’s crowbar or relying on a dumb AI to not get hit, and they will always find a way to get hit.

And since you don’t get a lot of healing herbs either – this is a problem.

You could grind away lower difficulty levels for more ammo and then switch to Hardcore, but then it feels like cheating. So unless you play in co-op – this game is just badly designed with artificial difficulty that relies on the AI. There are also sections where, in order to save ammo, you’d have to kite enemies as 1 character and do something else as the other, which further makes me believe that Survival is only reasonably playable on 1st playthrough in co-op.

[b]- Inconsistent[/b]
Mechanics don’t always work in a consistent manner. Headshots won’t always stun regular enemies, which is a problem when game expects you to save ammo for bullet-spongy bosses. Some areas can be explored by boosting a character upwards, but some areas with same-looking access can’t – they are scripted to be explored in a different manner.

[h1]Lowdown[/h1]
The 2 duos offer different playstyles and while I liked mission design for Clair and Moira more, Barry and Natalia make for a more fun gameplay. Overall, I think Revelations 2 straddles the line between being tedious like Revelations 1 and genuinely tense and engaging like RE4 or 5, but also is a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with how little ammo it sometimes gives you and how tight of an environment it forces you to fight in. This on top of zombies and other enemies being very quick makes for a tension that feels artificial. Mechanical tension, if you will, and that’s not how I believe horror games should make you feel.

Look at Dead Space 1 and 2. They don’t have super-tight environments or janky AI and they give you all the ammo you need. If you want an action horror – why make the game janky on purpose?

Would I recommend Revelations 2 more than RE 4 and 5? No. How about RE6? I honestly don’t know, since 6 had some very nice ideas and while it didn’t feel much like an RE game, neither does Revelations 2.

I'd give RE Revelations 2 as a whole (including all episodes) a
[h1]5/10[/h1]
I’ve had more fun with this than with RE 7 and about half of Village combined, but I struggle to decide whether I’d prefer to replay this or RE6, which makes me realize that RE series as it stands nowadays just isn’t for me anymore.

I hope someone will pick up the pieces and re-vitalize the dead survival-horror genre.

I'll need to finish the game for a full review but right off the bat, you can see how improved it is over the first game in the series.

Rev 2 actually feels like a full console/PC third person shooter. The graphics were bumped up and a whole bunch of new features were added, many similar to RE 4. Obviously, it was designed for much more powerful hardware at the time.

The game also focuses a lot more on bringing back horror with much better zombies and creatures, along with satisfying combat and animations.

I might be alone on this, but the game gives me some Alan Wake vibes when it comes to the engine and environment, but with zombies. I like it.

The co-op system is wayyyy better than that trash in Res 5 and since it's a third person shooter, makes it a lot more entertaining than in RE 0.

The transitioning between characters is smooth and both teams compliment each other well. 

Also.. two badass characters returning. Barry and Claire.

Another decent new story plot unrelated to the previous as well.

Now, you can see where the budget was limited with certain things like a generic inventory and the UI, but at least they kept the core feature-set like combining items to craft.

Also.. I think this is the only RE title where you can sneak, kill enemies from behind, dodge, and use an unbreakable knife.

They took elements of the old games and merged it with elements of 6 and 5, along with an improved co-op system like in Zero, except unlike all three of those games, it all came out pretty damn enjoyable.

The episodic release cycle was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid and Capcom should never do it again but since I bought the whole series this week and could play through everything without waiting, I won't count that in my review.

So far, it seems like a Revelations 3 is certainly something that needs to happen.

Update: Overall, I still like the game. A few caveats and issues they should have fixed.

Most notably the sneaking system which is pretty much broken. Considering the game focuses on it so heavily and it is actually required for two characters, i honestly don't understand how that got past quality control.

Second, the scripted events were a bit much... a major reason i believe the sneaking mechanic breaks or appears broken so often as well.

I don't usually give reviews but I thought I'd make an exception this time around. I remember hearing a lot about this game, most of it not good, I heard people say the first Revelations is good but not to bother with the second one, and so for a long time I didn't. Looking back, it's a real shame I listened because Revelations 2 is a fun time to be had, and personally, I can't help but feel that this is more a survival horror game than the first one, which after playing this one, definitely feels more action-oriented. The story, while convoluted (but what RE narrative isn't convoluted) is interesting and one that'll easily hook you in, the gameplay is obviously a lot like the first but plays out more methodically and reminds me of the original Resident Evil's, especially with the backtracking done throughout Barry's campaign, which, I know a lot of people won't like, but Barry's sections were a lot better to me than Claire's, not to say anything bad about Claire's, just that the backtracking's well done (as to be expected from RE), and the environments are some of my favorites throughout the whole series. That being said, however, this game has some terrible lag/frame drops, my PC should easily be able to run this game with the highest graphical settings, but even with them at the lowest it seems it can't handle more than three enemies on screen at once, I can't emphasize it enough, it can become extremely problematic, to the point where I looked everywhere for an anti-lag but with no luck, a lot of people also seem to share this issue while others don't experience anything at all, I definitely recommend this game (unless you plan to play co-op because the secondary characters don't have any reliable way to defend themselves) but if you have the option to play it on Playstation or XBOX, I'd recommend playing it there because it can truly be maddening sometimes, which is a shame because otherwise it's a great survival horror experience.


And for any newcomers to the franchise, don't worry about not being able to follow the story, there's a lot of references to older games in this one but they're just that: references. Almost every game in the franchise is a self-contained story that doesn't require you to play any previous outings to understand what's going on.

I bought this game and Resident Evil Revelations on sale, having only played them briefly on the DS and PS4, and not being too impressed with the graphics. The PC version of this game (both games) is absolutely phenomenal, however, and a must-play for any Resident Evil fan. 

The shooting is great and the enemies are super creepy! You can upgrade your weapons and switch up your loadout for different playstyles. You also control two characters this time, Claire and Moira, as well as Barry and Natalia. They all have their own personalities, and bits of ridiculous dialogue, but the story is surprisingly good. I especially loved Barry's sections, as he was my favorite character in the first Resident Evil game. 

There is a lot of replay value in the campaign but even more in Raid Mode. You can play as multiple different characters with different costumes, unlock weapons, perks, etc. There are also tons of levels, objectives, and difficulties. In my opinion Raid Mode offers much more than Mercenaries mode ever did. And I personally like it more than Mercenaries mode now. 

The environments are really cool too, I don't want to spoil anything. But the campaign (and Raid Mode) covers a lot of ground and I found myself taking screenshots constantly during both Claire and Barry's sections. 

Long story short: if you skipped over this game like me, definitely check it out! You will not be disappointed!

Resident Evil: Revelations 2 is an episodic RE game and sequel to RE: Revelations, set after RE5 but before RE6. If you're planning to buy this game without any DLC because of it's extremely cheap price during a sale, DON'T. I've seen many people made this mistake, if you just buy the game without any DLCs you'll only be able to play the first episode and Raid Mode. All other story content (episodes 2-4 and 2 extra episodes) are unlocked by buying the DLC. That being said, I do think this game is overpriced. Even on sale, the later episodes each cost like 4 times the price of the first one.

RE:R2 marks the return of characters from early RE games, Claire Redfield and Barry Burton. However, these characters aren't partners, Claire is with Moira and Barry with Natalia. In each episode, you start as Claire/Moira first, and the second part you play as Barry/Natalia. Many areas of Barry's level are the ones Claire went through first, but there are still plenty unique areas only traveled with one pair of protagonists, so don't be afraid about the game feeling repetitive. Sometimes, an action you make as Claire/Moira will affect the level that Barry/Natalia goes through.

Even though RE games where your characters have partners has been going on since RE5, a unique feature here is that you can change characters anytime you want. Claire/Barry are fighters with their numerous weapons, while Moira/Natalia are supports, able to find hidden items and go to places the fighters cannot. They can still fight, but nowhere as good as the Claire/Barry. Inventory management is a thing again, since you can craft items and key items take up a single inventory space. You can use the other character's inventory as extra storage, though.

The Raid Mode in RE:R2 is mostly the same, but quite easier than RE:R. One difference it has is the fact that every character has separate leveling, so if you keep playing as 1 character, the others will be stuck at level 1. The locations also has more variety, using modified maps from RE6 as well. There is no longer any pesky "no hit" medal, and it was replaced by "no healing items". Sadly despite being easier and more fun, Raid Mode only has very few, very easy achievements, unlike RE:R where half of the achievements are for Raid Mode.

After finishing an episode you'll be able to play the episode in either Countdown Mode or Invisible Mode. In Countdown, you'll have to break time bonuses and kill enemies to keep going. In Invisible Mode, enemies can only be seen by the support characters. To be honest, I'm not really a fan of how many achievements require all episodes to be replayed in both of these modes, and obtaining all medals by performing certain actions in an episode. It's difficult and repetitive, while strangely the extra episodes don't have achievements.

Resident Evil: Revelations 2 is a good, albeit overpriced RE game. It would be a lot better if each episode has the same price as the first one, since the game is not really that long. It's better to buy the Deluxe Edition instead of purchasing only story DLCs separately, since the price difference isn't that big. If you're a fan of the early RE protagonists like Claire and Barry, you should definitely buy this game.

This game has been a very positive surprise for me. For a cheap, kind of forgotten game in the series, I had low expectations, but Resident Evil Revelations 2 has turned out to be a great game, one of the best in the series in my opinion.

Revelations 2 is a huge improvement on Revelations 1. Graphics, storyline and overall playability have all been improved on extensively. The game has a very well made co-op mode, and even a very well working split-screen possibility where another player can jump in and out easily. This game has huge replay value, since there are different choices to be made and routes you can take on another playthrough. Also, after each episode you get a ranking and points to be used in an in-game store, which furthermore adds to the game's replay value.

In addition to the main story, like in the first Revelations game, there's a raid mode that has a huge amount of content. A lot of different customizable weapons and a huge amount of maps and a lot of enemies, some of which aren't even present in the main campaign. A wide range of playable characters as well, each with unique skills and a level-up system. There are also daily missions and weekly events. It's actually so great, that I wonder why Capcom hasn't included this kind of a mode in the newer RE games. This game has so much extra content that RE 2 & 3 Remakes pale in comparison.

For a very low price, you can at the very least purchase Episode 1 and try it out. Otherwise I would recommend you to buy the whole game. With the very well made and thought-out Raid mode, it's almost as if it's two games for the price of one.

So glad I decided to dive into the remaining RE titles I didn't get to complete way back because of the whole episodic nonsense. This game, much like Revelations 1 goes for the episodic story vibe but does it in a better way I felt. Revelations one decided to divvy up every Episode into 3 acts, such as Episode 1, Chapter 1, 2, 3, etc, this one just has Episode 1 and then 2 acts that are pretty lengthy. 

So what's the story? Claire and Moira are part of an organization whom seemingly randomly is under attack, both characters are knocked out and taken prisoner on a very hostile island as part of some weird science game or murder and zambonis. Likewise, once completing Act 1, which is usually the Claire/Moira sections, in Act 2 - you play as Barry Burton and a little girl called Natalia that has special abilities with the kicker being that Barry's acts cover the same grounds, more or less, as Claire and Moira do, but some months later. This creates a weird, but cool dynamic that also affects gameplay but creates 2 separate styles. Claire's sections are more akin to the SAW films while Barry's sections feel like more traditional Resident Evil with a splash of Evil Within (yes I mean this unironically). 

Gameplay wise! Something I failed to mention in my past Revelations review, is something I found kinda funky with both titles in comparison to Resident Evil 6, which were these games' mother title - and that boils down to feedback. In RE6 and below to boot, when you shot an enemy in the head, you'd see them react erratically, or even sometimes have their heads just go pop - that is entirely missing in Rev 1 and Rev 2, which makes it feel clunky, but the same mechanics apply. You can score Critical Hits on enemies but damage seems to be much more flat, instead relying more on the upgrade system both games have - which is to say, you find parts that can increase a weapon's base damage, ammo capacity, recoil, etc, you use those on weapons and each weapon has a limited number of slots to take in parts - this ended up making exploration a HUGE part of Rev 2 and consequently made the game very, very easy. 

As far as the actual per character mechanics go - Claire and Moira are both a lot more undergeared than Barry is and by extension you get a lot less weapon parts to work with, these acts rely a lot more on puzzle solving and sometimes even hard promotes running away from mobs to not waste ammo, which was very scarce in these acts - however the enemies you fight for the most part, are very easy to take down and instead rely more on ganging up on you. On the opposite spectrum, Barry and Natalia have a LOT more to them - Barry comes pre-equipped with an Assault Rifle, the best handgun in the game and a Magnum meanwhile Natalia is able to sense where enemies are which leads to some pretty tense moments and makes the game a lot more stealth friendly. The enemies on Barry's side however, are MUCH stronger and a lot more varied, they don't gang up on you, but a single enemy can take up a lot of resources if not handled well.

An issue I did have with the game, Claire's sections can drag on a fair bit mostly because it's a lot of puzzles in sequence, and some of them can be a little hard to figure out the first time around - so pacing issues are bound to pop up. 

I think even with the pacing issues, the game ended up feeling fairly short, however, it's a game very much worth playing if you love Resident Evil. I do think the large enemy variety, the much more oppressive atmosphere and the characters are better handled than the first Revelations title, however pacing issues and the story resolving two acts at the same time missed a little for me.

I cannot begin to express how much I loved this game; Before I begin this review I'd like to make it clear that I rarely buy games directly from steam. I'd much rather buy super cheap bundles but in this case I bought the game directly from steam along with episode 2, 3 and 4.

I'll break this review up into sections to effectively express how much I loved this game while also allowing myself to focus on some of the drawbacks as well.

This is not a flawless game but I think it's worth every penny.

[h2]Controls[/h2]

The controls are, at the best of times, pretty much perfect and flow without a hitch and, at the worst of times, a minor inconvenience. Occasionally you'll find yourself finding a new weapon, swapping it with an old one, only to pick the old one up again because your interact keys, E and F, can also be done just by left-clicking. The settings menu can be a little difficult to navigate at times as well as assigned keys but these can all be changed in their respective keyboard / controller layout menu. I'd recommend swapping your running from toggle to hold as it, at least in my case, made the game feel a lot better but again this was just personal preference.

[h2]Voice Acting[/h2]

The voice acting in RER2 is superb. Particularly Michael McConnohie, the voice of Barry Burton and a veteran of the business and Gabrielle Pastore, the voice of Natalia Korde, work amazingly together displaying immense amounts of chemistry in their dialogue. Every line, whimper and scream is delivered with pure conviction and authenticity.

The final interaction between Moira and Claire in Episode 4, without spoiling anything here, is intense. It's something I couldn't expect and something I wish I had've had more time to process.

[h2]Visuals and Graphics[/h2]

The character models, scenery, terrain etc. are all amazing; It's dark, gritty and, at times, feels more like a horror game than a survival. How the virus interacts with certain enemies after you've shot them [spoiler]the black tentacle thing wrapped around where you shot[/spoiler] is an awesome detail and one I'm glad they added. The bosses are horrifying, abominations of flesh and bone which I wasn't ready for in the slightest and couldn't help but appreciate the effort of the design team.

The only complaint, if I had to include one, is that when characters are talking occasionally the mouth / face interacts weirdly and out-of-sync with dialogue in a motion similar to chewing with your mouth as widely open as you can. It doesn't always happen but when it does it kinda snaps you out of the trance the game puts you in.

The cinematics make up for any drawbacks that may happen particularly the final cinematic of Barry and Natalia's campaign in episode 4. It's art.

[h2]Story[/h2]

Now. This is why you buy RER2.

The story is unbelievably brilliant. It does take some time to kick-off but once the ball starts rolling it's like an avalanche of emotions. Like a boa it wraps you and holds you so tight to the point that you'll never forget what happened.

I'll include a full spoiler at the bottom because I'd like to discuss the ending.

[h2]Overall Rating and Feelings[/h2]

The game is amazing. As my first game in the Resident Evil Franchise I think it was an amazing place to start and one I'd highly recommend to others.

[b][u]Below are my scoring out of 10 for each category[/u][/b]

Controls: [spoiler]8/10[/spoiler]
Voice Acting: [spoiler]10/10[/spoiler]
Visuals and Graphics: [spoiler]9/10[/spoiler]
Story: [spoiler]10/10[/spoiler]

Total Rating: [spoiler]9.25/10[/spoiler]

[h2]Massive Spoilers Ahead! I will be discussing the endings[/h2]

[spoiler]The final episode, "Metamorphosis", concludes with one of two endings. In my first playthrough Alex successfully transfers her consciousness into Natalia and effectively becomes reborn. 

Natalia is no more. 

It was heart-wrenching to watch. Barry becomes her adoptive father, you, as the player, build a true connection between them. You watch Barry come to terms with the death of his blood, Moira, only to watch his newly "adoptive" daughter disappear before his very eyes. 

The villain wins.

That's what hurts the most. 

Sure Claire survives the ordeal but what's left of them. Claire couldn't save Moira despite how close they were to surviving [b]together[/b] and Barry has lost both his daughters. He never got to apologise to Moira. He heard her weak and trembling voice over the phone and knew she was gone.

The second ending is worth every fibre of the effort it takes in the play-through. If you make Moira shoot "corrupted-neil" instead of Claire you get an equally perfect ending. 

Moira survives being crushed by rocks and saves Natalia. Barry is reunited with his, believed to be deceased, daughter and there's an immediate release of tension despite the situation. Mutated Alex becomes more and more mangled to the point of being a black, mutilated corpse fuelled by nothing more than rage and revenge. Claire returns with a helicopter and sniper rifle to assist Barry in his efforts and you're given one last boss fight.

It's tremendous and an experience unlike any other. It's beyond perfect.

Even the final cutscene fills your mind with possible situations and outcomes; Is Natalia really Natalia or is she still part of Alex? Will everything go back to normal?

It's hard to say but one thing is clear:

Capcom have made one of the greatest video game stories that I've ever had the pleasure of playing.
[/spoiler]

[h2]EDIT[/h2]

I've included an edit to go over the raid mode since I forgot to include it in my initial review.

The raid mode is a solid addition to the game giving players, who choose not to buy the additional episodes, an avenue to keep themselves entertained. It's decently fun, challenging at times and overall a decently enjoyable experience. I'll be honest I don't even remotely understand how it's relevant to the context of RER2 but as a "mini-game" it's, as I said, a decently enjoyable experience.

It does become tedious at times but almost all games experience tedium at some point.

I'd rate the raid feature about: [spoiler]6/10[/spoiler]

Resident Evil Revelations 2 was one of those games I didn’t expect much from, and then it completely impressed me. The episodic structure actually fits the pacing well — short, focused chapters that give you just enough tension and story to keep going. The alternating perspective between Claire/Moira and Barry/Natalia is one of the strongest design choices: you see one event, then later understand the consequences from the other side. It creates this great slow-burn mystery vibe.

Gameplay-wise, it strikes a very satisfying balance between survival horror and modern controls. Ammo isn’t overly generous, enemies hit hard, and there are plenty of moments where you panic-reload or regret wasting bullets earlier. The partner mechanics are surprisingly fun: one character handles the weapons while the other supports with scanning, spotting enemies, or using basic improvised attacks. It sounds odd on paper, but in co-op or even solo, it gives encounters more strategy than just “shoot everything.”

It’s not flawless — a few encounters repeat themselves, some dialogue is unintentionally cheesy, and certain stealth sections can be irritating — but none of that ruins the experience.

Overall, this game delivers great atmosphere, strong pacing, and tons of replay value. For me, it stands comfortably as one of the best Resident Evil entries outside the main numbered line — second place in my personal ranking, right behind RE2 Remake.

If you’re a fan of the franchise or survival horror in general, this one is absolutely worth playing.

Resident Evil Revelations 2 Review

You are in for one hell of a night!

Some key points that this game offers:

1.	Episodic play style
2.	Claire and Barry are Back
3.	New game mechanics
4.	Character Swap
5.	New enemy types
6.	Assistive Co-op

Gameplay & Controls:

Big Brother, Resident Evil! You awake to find yourself trapped, there are camera’s everywhere and a strange host… The staff are all a new breed of Zombies and there are some new BOW supervisors… The goal; survive this new hell, when all is set against you!

Quite the step up from RE Revelations one. Combat and controls feel smoother this time around. There are also some new mechanics present as well. Stealth plays a vital role this time. Sneak up on enemies for maximum damage. This greatly helps when bullets are scarce, and if there is one thing that is always scarce, it is bullets! 

Melee also got buffed up this time, you can charge up your melee action for superior damage, and what’s more, is that you can co-op that melee with your AI partner to really put the hurt on these new Zombies.

The game boasts assistive co-op play. The campaign is still single player but you can swap between characters throughout the levels. At some points, you will not be able to proceed without swapping characters. Claire helps Moira up on broken ladders and Moira also packs a crowbar to pry open locked chests and doors. With Barry and Natalia, she is the only one that can fit through small openings to help proceed with the levels. Cleverly designed and it totally adds to the Survival Horror aspect since neither of the co-op sidekicks are particularly strong fighters.

There is an impressive skill list that you can upgrade and unlock as you progress through the campaign. These skills really up your zombie-stopping powers. Weapon mods are also back this time around allowing you to upgrade and improve your weapon potentials. 

Revelations 2 also follows the Episodic style that Revelations 1 did. I wasn’t too fond of the first one because there were too many characters and you just didn’t get enough playtime with them all. With Revelations 2 they actually improved that concept and brought it down to two characters; namely Claire and Barry. The game, however, only came out with Episode 1, with the second coming out a few weeks later.

Graphics:

The atmosphere was beautifully created to maintain the fact that this is a RE Horror title. The level layout was done brilliantly, the way the visuals tie in with the world itself is flawless and downright gorgeous. 

The new zombie types are quite hideous in their own right, they did a beautiful job with our new play mates. Let us not forget the other things that prowl about. They did a fantastic job to up the horror scale on these creatures.

Character design was done just as beautifully; Each character has their own distinct appearance and animations. Lightning and shadows play a brilliant role here, they enhance the experience completely and add to the immersion. 

Sounds:

Eerie, gloomy, and downright scary! Everything a RE fan wants and needs. There are sounds and shrieks for everything. You are never alone, nor do you feel alone, and that is only partly because of your ai partner. The sounds are the main player here, as they still make some strange noise in your ear to make you wonder what's around the corner!

As always the voice over artists did a stunning job with their voice over work. They brought these characters to life beautifully, adding depth, emotion, and a tone to them that fans would adore and totally love.

Replayability:

Once you played and finished the campaign, you play it again on the newly unlocked difficulties… There are a few this time around, so you are in for a real treat! Plus, the return of an older one too.

Rain mode got a massive overhaul! There are new characters, new weapons, and pretty much new everything. As new episodes are released so will their respective raid mode stages.

Update: With the final episodes released for the game, Raid mode now boasts over 15 characters and over 200 raid mode stages. That’s an insane amount of content that will keep you busy for quite a while!

MGR Gaming’s Conclusions:
Spoilers Ahead:

Revelations 2 is truly an exceptionally great sequel to number 1. They fixed and improved a lot of mechanics that were lacking in Revelations 1.

The new Raid mode was a huge step forward, with so much new content that you'll get completely lost in it. The Levels in the campaign mode are longer than they were in Revelations 1, but that is to be expected since this time around we only have two characters in the game, and the episodes are divided into two parts. Part one being Claire and Moira, and part two being Barry and Natalia.

I loved what they did with Revelations 2, the setting is perfect, the layout and gameplay are fantastic. The story is brilliantly written and plays beautifully. The only thing I didn’t really enjoy was that we had to buy and wait for the other episodes, this is the one thing that I didn’t really enjoy. Patience isn’t the issue, it’s the fact that we get 1/4th of a new game and had to wait weeks for the rest to be released. 

The new zombie types again give us new reasons to fear and dread. These are no ordinary zombies though; a new virus gives them some intelligence and manoeuvrability. They can and do use weapons if they have them, some crawl, and others can even run towards you, and these are only the basic ones. The BOW monsters are a whole other ball game waiting on you!  

I really enjoyed seeing Claire in action again, the same goes for Barry, they were left dormant for way too long!
Update: Another neat feature that I enjoyed here was the time between the episode parts. Claire and Moira take place in what is the past, and with Barry and Natalia, it is six months later. What is neat here is how you can see what time has done to the place. Things rarely look the same when you visit an area that you played through with the other duo. 

They didn’t reuse the same layouts either. Barry and Natalia make use of alternate routes most of the times adding new scenes to the game.

It's pretty good on average, but the parts where it doesn't work stick out like a sore thumb.

The core gameplay loop is good, and it stretches the RE formula in ways that feel interesting.

You have two teams, each of two characters, one with firearms and the other without. The AI isn't terrible, but it isn't going to win any "smarter than a brick" awards, and the best it can do is sort of keep itself out of danger.

There are mechanics based around shining a light or pointing a finger at search spots to expose hidden items, and it feels cool to scour your environment looking for hidden objects.

There's crafting, which is a little too limited and mostly clogs up your inventory, and there's stealth attacks, which the game sort of forces you to focus on due to ammo scarcity in the early chapters.

The gameplay is extremely linear, unlike most core RE games which have a little more of a puzzlebox feel, and there are light rpg elements which work extremely well.

The sound design is stellar, and the english translation takes such extraordinary liberties with the japanese script that it's almost a different story. This is a good thing, because the japanese script isn't great. It's hammy and saccharine, which clashes with the whole fighting-the-jigsaw-killer-in-the-hellraiser-dimension thing the rest of the game has going for it.

The spots where the game falls short, then, are pretty minor. But each one felt like tripping over a land mine.

There's some clunky, unexplained controls that you need to get through a certain part of the game if you're not two-playering it. I had to look these up online.

There's also a number of other instadeaths that don't feel especially earned. Certain enemy attacks will clip through cover, scratch you with a pixel, and kill you instantly while their animation glitches out and the game chugs.

Speaking of chugging, if your computer is on the older side, lighting up your flashlight will drop your framerate into the negatives. Especially if there's water around. I had to spend most of my time in the sewer level staring at walls and waiting for the game to stop coughing out its engine.

So ultimately, if you like your Resident Evil a little experimental and you don't mind a bit of jank to the gameplay, I think this is pretty fun.

I wouldn't pick it over four, or seven, or one remake, or two remake, or revelations one, but it leads a lot of the rest of the pack.

Claire and Moira get stranded on a death island full of bio-weapon horrors and have to survive while wearing these bracelets that track their fear, if they become too afraid their bodies mutate turning them into monsters, now they have to fight to survive the island of living hell. Meanwhile Barry Burton explores the island six months later looking for his daughter and finds Natalia, a mysterious little girl with a strange ability to see enemies through walls as well as invisible ones. 3. Each chapter you will start playing as Claire and Moira then switch to Barry and Natalia six months later. The veil on why Claire and Moira as well as Natalia are there is slowly lifted as you go through this island of death and find out who or what is behind it all. The ending is satisfying (stay after credits) with an ending that hints at characters from Resident Evil 6 and has a little extra cheekiness that may or may not be followed up on in the future. Overall a phenomenal game, 8.5/10 better than first Revelations in my eyes, though its not bad stand alone, you'll definitely get more mileage if you played the other RE games, specifically 1,2, and Revelations 1.

This review will be divided into sections, since the game has different modes which vary greatly.

Main Campaign:
Revelations 2 has an ok campaign with branching paths, and allows you to make actions to influence the next scenario, the changes range from a new route to skipped enemies, there are quite a few places that influence this which I really liked.
The episodic nature of the campaign makes you think that they will be longer campaigns, but they are actually shorter than you expect, my first playthrough on the game's equivalent for hard took around 10 hours without help, and subsequent runs took like 4 hours after you know the solution to the puzzles and surprise enemy ambushes. The difficulty starts to really ramp up on hard which is the difficulty I picked at the start, ammo is scarse, and you may end up with only your knife and crowbar to deal with the enemies, plus since the enemies don't drop any goods at all, avoid baddies when possible is a viable strategy.
The main campaign and the extra non raid modes all share a skill system which unlock certain abilities and passives that help you through the journey, presented in a small tree, the difference between a fresh start and when you have all skills is HUGE, animation cancel makes the game feel much more smooth but comes at a huge cost, just the fact of getting that skill (which costs 10000 Skill PPoints) means that you will have to do heavy grinding for points if you want to have maxed characters, which helps a lot in the DLC's and in the 4th unlockable difficulty.
Certain skills feel really meh though, like the one that allows AI controlled characters to shoot without consuming ammo, they either don't shoot at all, or they deal absolutely no noticeable damage, even with a magnum they can't stagger the weakest rotten enemy...
But when you find out that Moira can regen health but Claire cannot, you feel like you played the whole game wrong, Moira can mostly go forward and beat ♥♥♥♥ up with the crowbar, and if she goes down, Claire can revive her infinitely to full health.
Oh and we get to see the return of beloved classic characters Claire Redfield and Barry Burton which is a plus

The Struggle:
The name should be the frustration, this mini episode introduces a gimmick of limited continues, if you die you need to spend 50 meat to retry, and when you run out of animal meat you restart the whole thing. And instead of Claire, now the main character is Moira, so say goodbye to her infinite regenerating health, now the partner is the old man from the sewers and he is pretty much Moira mk2 which can actually wield guns, and regens ammo between chapters.
This dlc is composed of 4 stages, 2 about scavenging and 2 survivals, in scavenging you have a certain amount of time to hunt animals and gather ammo and resources, while on the survival sections you have to face against a set number of enemies in closed areas of the map, you beat all the enemies? you get teleported to the next one, repeat a few times and it's done.
The first scavenging gives you ample time and is really easy, First survival you need to make shots count and dodge properly as Moira's resources carry over and you fight a lot of the fat fire guys, Ironheads, and quite a few of the common infected. Second scavenging mission is frustration incarnate, now you go through a Revenant filled Fishing Village and Moira/Evgeny have to stealth kill them, else, for some reason I still can't comprehend, the mission time gets reduced to 30 seconds, and have to make a run for it, what is infuriationg you ask? The range for stealth attacks is totally bugged in this mode, you can easily do stealth kills in campaign but here they randomly don't work, and going through the village is hell without killing the Revenants, plus sometimes a revenant spawns in the middle of the village that doesn't move at all, and is not there at the beggining... Second Survival is a pure resource check, you either have enough bullets and firebombs here or it's hell, as about half the enemies here are Revenants with the Catapult like ones, a few Durgas mixed in and you can't see the weak points with neither character here. To beat this mode you need to be very stingy with resources, and not ragequit in the bugged Fishing scavenge. 

Little Miss:
Metal Gear Solid ft Natalia, you go forward without being seen by the enemies, and the companion here is a Dark Natalia which is completely invisible to enemies, and serves as a recon unit, not too hard and no limited continues, much more enjoyable than The Struggle

Raid Mode:
A very grindy mess with flaws handcrafted by Capcom just so they can sell you the solution with more DLC, you want the OP campaign animation cancel? Buy Wesker DLC and inherit the AC, want to become invisible and stealth kill most normal enemies? Buy Hunk DLC and inherit Cloak, want to actually upgrade parts like the game wants you too? better buy the Parts storage DLC so you can have parts of multiple levels to actually combine them afterwards, just remember that some parts have 20 levels, and you have only 75 slots for different parts, and each level counts as a different part so...
The weapon and Album storage ones are much less useful, album is nearly worthless imo, so if you want to seriously play Raid Mode here, just ignore those 2 and buy 1 Parts storage dlc or 2, but remember that Capcom created these limitations and sold you the solution, if you want to support those practices, you do you. I just skipped raid mode in this game for these reasons, and a few more.
They raised level caps to 100 and all characters need to be leveled separately, this makes the mode extremly grindy if you want to see every unique skill and eventually inherit them to other characters.
Plus they have limited capabilities at the start, some can only wield 1 or 2 weapons and need to level a lot to wield 3 and eventually 4, just because of this you may run out of ammo to kill enemies in the early levels.
And Skills also need to be unlocked, leveled up, then inherited for other chars to use, all of this costs Skill Points, and you only get them with each level up, so the level of grind starts to reminisce of an MMO.
And one last offender, in this game you either lose the weapons or the attached parts, but not both, so one mistake and you might need to destroy either, so be 100% of what to equip to your weapons, this wasn't a thing in the original raid mode, and people told me this was removed on the Switch version, I mean even the campaign allows you to remove parts, wtf capcom...
And now there are 4 difficulties for each map, each with faster enemies with more modifiers, hell even the basic rotten enemies become Usain Bolt at Code Red difficulty.
Maps come from Revelations 2 and Resident Evil 6, and thanks to the 4 difficulties, expect to see them a lot.
If you can tolerate how grindy this mode is, you may have quite some fun with the different characters, the different enemy modifiers, the new parts, the mix of enemies, the QoL improvements like how now you don't need to run Ghost Ship without being hit once to get the rarest parts, since now parts come in easy to access boxes in the level, and requirement for completion bonus is to not use herbs, not to not get hit even once like in revelations 1, actual split screen local play, and probably a few more that I forgot

In conclusion, do I recommend Revelations 2? Yes on the Campaign, Not really on The Struggle, Yes-ish on Little Miss, and No on Raid Mode, unless you can tolerate capcom's greed with the Raid Mode DLC, and enjoy grinding for some reason.

On February 3rd 2026 Capcom released an update that removed Denuvo from RE4 Remake, a DRM which requires a costant internet connection, and replaced it with the Enigma Protector. This DRM is supposed to prevent "cheating" (any kind of modding of the game) and it's russian developed.
Tested by the Youtube channel Digital Foundry in the video "Resident Evil 4 PC: Is New DRM Impacting Game Performance?" has been found that the Enigma Protector DRM causes an average of -10% in framerate drops, with dips of -40% in certain scenarios, way more than the original Denuvo DRM.

This is not the first time that Capcom decided to put Enigma in some of their older games: RE Revelations suffered major backlash from customers because of the major dip in perfomance, so much so they had to remove Enigma from the game for good and recently they released the original Dino Crisis series on Steam, a quick scouring of the forum will reveal a lot of customers unhappy with the perfomance of said games. Why a 25 years old single player game that should run flawlessly on a phone had to be "protected" against "cheating" is everyone's guess, especially when you realise that a GOG version of both games was already available, without the Enigma Protector and without issues.

Resident Evil Revelations 2 is a survival horror game.
Claire Redfield and the daughter of Barry Burton, Moira, got knocked out and kidnapped. After awakening they find themselves in a dark and abandoned detention facility on a remote island.
Barry is going on search for Moira a few months later.
Players will play through areas in different timelines. The first half of a chapter with Claire and Moira and the second part with Barry and Natalia (a girl who was found on the island).
Players will need to switch between the two characters (Claire/Moira, Barry/Natalia) during the gameplay to proceed.
Revelations 2 consists of 4 Episodes, 1 Episode has a duration of something under 2 hours.
The story is not really spectacular, so it is fine by me that it does not take long to finish it.
The campaign can be played in local coop on splitscreen or it can be played online with Remote Play (setting it up is a bit annoying and 2 gamepads are required for the host).
Besides of the campaign there is also The Raid mode which can be played normaly online.
The graphics are not so good, it could have been way more better.
The music and voice acting is okay. Claire has a new voice here.
Some people have reported they have problems to launch the game, they have a black screen at launch. There are a few fixes in the discussions, like editing the config file. I also had problems with a black screen but for me the fix was simply to unplug my keyboard (a Corsair) before starting the game to make it work (weird...).
Overall, Resident Evil Revelations 2 is okay, it is not one of the best games in the Resident Evil series but also definitely not one of the worst. If you like the Resident Evil games you should get Revelations 2 during a sale, the regular price for all chapters is too much.

The game is actually scary! Mostly, just the first two episodes but yeah.

Fan favorite characters Claire and Barry are back with new side characters Moira and Natalia. The side characters can be manually controlled to see hidden objects and hidden enemies and they can't use guns which is an innovative new mechanic. It's also a good thing the team is smaller this time for the characters to actually develop, unlike in Rev 1 where you played with a bunch of new idiots every episode nobody cares about. But to be honest, these old and new characters don't do much in terms of character development other than Barry and Moira.

Claire is your stoic and goody no-nonsense action cop, i like her design she looks older and more experienced also i love the fact that the developers kept her pure and well spoken but other than that she's very boring. Moira is your average millenial edgy young adult who says F.ck every sentence and "hates" old men including her own father. Barry is Joel from the Last of Us and Natalia is your stereotypical sweet and innocent little girl who doesn't know anything and you should feel pity for... I know, you shouldn't expect well written characters in "B-MOVIE RE GAMES" but this game tries so hard to be like a TV show and pretentious by contiounsly quoting famous literature works just like the first Revelations.

The story is about Claire and Moira getting kidnapped to an island near Russia where they are used for an experiment along with other members from this new "anti-terrorist" organization TerraSave... RE lore that nobody cares about just like the first Revelations but whatever. The island has an "overseer" which is the main villain and i won't spoil who it is but it's imo the WORST RE VILLAIN in HISTORY, i'd rather have that opera leech guy from RE 0. Claire, Moira and the others on the island are infected with a new virus called T-phobos which reacts to the fear meter on their bracelet, sort of like in a Saw movie, if it turns red they mutate into a zombie, which is what happened to all of the survivors throughout the game except for, you guessed it, Claire and Moira. See i can understand Claire for being experienced with surviving zombie outbreaks and whatever but Moira? The whole subplot about the bracelet gets dropped after Episode 2. Then Barry and Natalia's story takes place 6 months after Claire and Moira disappeared, so now the game turns into The Last of Us with a bad story.

The good thing is that Barry and Natalia work well together, cause some of the enemies have invisible weak points or are completely invisible which only Natalia can point out for Barry to shoot at. It's a really cool mechanic but this is where the flaws come in... Natalia can't attack enemies other than throw a brick, which sure helps distracting them for a while but if you're out of bullets with just your knife as a weapon, you're in for a frustrating time because of how unbalanced the game is. Just like in RE 5 your ammo and items stack up with each chapter but in this game you don't get ammo for killing enemies, you're forced to look for them and be conservative because in each episode ammo is very scarce especially on normal or higher difficulties basically forcing you to replay the same episodes over and over just for some ammo. My recommendation would be to finish the game on Easy first then get the unlimited rocket launcher then tackle the rest of difficulties by stacking up as much ammo as you can for a better score.

The story forces you to replay the same levels with Barry but by taking a different route with different and harder enemies which is a cool idea but that basically means 50% same content and 50% new content in each episode. This works in Episode 1 and 2 because the areas you're in get enough time for you to explore and get immersed in, The Prison is still my favorite part of the game because of this and the Forest was also pretty good. But in Episodes 3 and 4 you just get through different building and areas filled with the same enemies then up to the next area all in the same episode which makes them feel repetitive and not scary. 

There is no detailed map other than a minimap which isn't always clear and might end up with you running in circles also these crappy levels are very limited because, once you acces a new section of the level the game goes through a long loading time animation, autosaves the checkpoint and then you can't go back to the previous section in case you forgot something, then you'll have to quit and replay the whole episode again. The game also has a lot of padding going on, like the medals in each episode are mostly the same and some are even ridiculous to perform without some Youtube video explaining how to get them. But you'll need these in case you want 100% achievments like me, another example for some dumb reason you unlock rewards by completing the levels and certain requierements then you have to buy those same rewards afterwards with Battle Points for you to use them in game... The padding is real.

Finally Raid mode is not much better than it was in Rev 1, in contrary, i found it to be boring but some might like it. Overal, if you enjoyed Revelations 1, 4 or even 6 you might enjoy Revelations 2. If you only like Classic RE then stay away from this game!

[h1]Resident Evil Burnout[/h1]
Disclaimer: I played Resident Evil 4, Resident Evil: Revelations, and Resident Evil: Revelations 2 in succession. So, while my overall experience and remarks about this game are positive, I do believe that I began to experience a bit of burnout with the Resident Evil franchise while playing this game. As a consequence, my play sessions became very short and sporadic for several weeks until I mustered up the energy to plow through the majority of the game in a couple of days. 

[h1]Improvements over Revelations 1[/h1]
That said, after my experience with the first Revelations game, I came in expecting pleasant mediocrity, but Revelations 2 turned out to be a far better game than I expected. It’s better than the first Revelations game in almost every way. 

The environments are actually dark and spooky. The soundtrack pairs well with the environments to supplement the spooky vibe. In the first Revelations game, the guns sounded like toys. In Revelations 2, the guns sound significantly better. They sound like actual guns, and I enjoyed using pretty much all of them. 

The level design is far better. The first Revelations was really hindered by its initial launch on the 3DS. The levels in Revelations 1 were obnoxiously littered with doors to cordon off little digestible sections for the hardware of the 3DS. For Revelations 2, it feels more akin to a late PS3-era game, rather than a portable/mobile game. 

The UI is also significantly better than Revelations 1. It actually feels like I’m looking at something designed by someone with UX experience, rather than a 140p YouTube video from 2005. 

Sadly, this game still doesn’t support ultrawide resolutions, so I had to play this at the measly resolution of 2560x1440. I know...just unplayable. /s

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
I planned to play this game in co-op with a friend, but we decided against that. Even with Steam Remote Play Together, it’s just not up to what we’d come to expect from the co-op of Resident Evil 5 and 6. The co-op in Revelations 2 is, in my opinion, [url=https://i.imgur.com/zV31yu6.jpg]an unplayable split screen resolution[/url]. 

Revelations 2 consists of four chapters, each with an A and B side and two playable characters per A/B side, [spoiler]taking place months apart from one another.[/spoiler] During a given A/B side of a chapter, you can switch back and forth, at will, between characters, which creates a pretty interesting gameplay dynamic. For each A/B side, only one character is really proficient in combat, while the other can more easily detect enemies and items. The Genesis gun from Revelations 1 is gone, but the Batman Detective Mode™ is back in spades, as only Moira or Natalia can detect useful items hidden in plain sight. Moira sensibly does this by using her Alan Wake™ flashlight. Natalia...she just points at things. 

Initially, I tried playing this on the hardest difficulty, Survival. That lasted a total of 20 minutes. I’m not sure if it was the ammo scarcity, the high damage output of enemies, the two characters you had to manage HP for simultaneously, or just that I was burned out on the Resident Evil franchise in general, but I just couldn’t do it, so I bumped it down to Normal, which left me with a more action-oriented Resident Evil game, albeit, a Resident Evil game with significantly more dark and atmospheric areas than the first Revelations, or Resident Evil 5, or 6. 

Stealth is supposedly an actual mechanic in this game. Supposedly, you can actually avoid enemies without having to waste precious ammo on encounters, but I was honestly only ever able to achieve this while playing with Barry, and I think I only stealth killed 3 or 4 enemies. Maybe I’m just terrible, but in my opinion, the stealth in this game is not exactly well implemented. 

The inventory and gun upgrade systems in Revelations 2 are practically identical to the first Revelations. The way that health restoration items work has been improved...by restoring how it worked in Resident Evil 4, 5, and 6. Red herbs are back, and now again combine with one green herb to produce three green herbs. There’s no longer a total max of five green herbs. Instead, there’s a stack max of five green herbs, and you can have as many stacks of five as your inventory will allow, which I think is more than fair. 

There’s also new bleeding and “gunk” status ailments in the game. Each of which you’ll have to craft and carry around unique healing items to cure. Although finding the components, crafting the healing items, and doing inventory management for them creates a challenging survival horror experience, I honestly found it a little annoying considering how rarely they’re needed and how completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ you are if you don’t have them. 

[h1]The Struggle[/h1]
This was the first of the two bonus episodes. There was no “Normal” difficulty, so I stooped down to the pro-gamer difficulty of Casual. With that said, I really didn’t have any issues with ammo conservation or the rations, which is food you have to scavenge to afford restarts after a death. This is undoubtedly more challenging on Survival difficulty, but as I said in the beginning, I was really burned out and just wanted to experience the story aspects of the DLC and honestly wasn’t interested in the challenge. 

This DLC focuses on Moira’s story between 4-1 and 4-2, but it honestly doesn’t show anything new. It retreads the literal same levels from the main campaign. It’s fast-paced. There’s story and shooting; that’s it. There’s no puzzle solving or platforming. After killing the required number of baddies, you just cut to the next area to commence the shooty shooty. It was honestly kinda fun though. 

[h1]Little Miss[/h1]
This one though...not fun. Again, it retreads the same exact levels from the main game. It follows Natalia between 1-1 and 1-2, but again provides no new information and is a story solely about Natalia finding her lost teddy bear, Lottie. This DLC also relies entirely on stealth, which I found to be a really weak aspect of the game. It did create some enjoyably tense moments while avoiding breaking stealth, but a teddy bear MacGuffin? 

[h1]Bugs and Annoyances[/h1]
[list]
[*]One time, at band camp, [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6L9KjD3FxOQ&feature=youtu.be]I had to throw a molotov at an enemy that spawned behind an unreachable room to progress the level.[/url]
[*]Another time, during the final section of the game, I died in the boss fight and respawned completely unable to move. This is unfortunately a well-documented bug dating back to 2015. I found [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/287290/discussions/0/611701360818755038/]a Steam Community thread about it[/url], and the fix was as simple and annoying as reducing your framerate to 30fps to spawn in, and then changing it back to 60/unlocked afterwards. 
[*]During the tower collapse sequence in 4-1, Jesus H. Chris, Claire and Moira sidle excruciatingly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow. 
[*]“I’m going to survive the ♥♥♥♥ out of this.” No real complaint here. Just thought this was a funny line.
[*]Occasionally, I feel like games are trying to teach me words to expand my vocabulary in unnecessary ways. Maybe the developers learned a new word and just wanted to share it with everyone. In Gears 5, I was taught about the architectural majesty of a GANTRY. In Uncharted 4, Nathan Drake taught me about the wonders of little piles of stones, called CAIRNS. In Revelations 2, Barry wouldn’t shut the ♥♥♥♥ up about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SLUICE. I didn’t know what it was before, I can guarandamntee I won’t remember it a week from now. 
[/list]
