So far pretty good (currently through episode 2)! I came into RE:R2 with pretty low expectations. I've played through most of the RE's and didn't really like the direction the series went with RE4, 5, 6 - being a fan of the slow paced fixed camera/tank control/very limited inventory system. The original Revelations was also just plain weird and over the top and wouldn't even feel like a RE game if it didn't have Jill and Chris in it.

That being said, Revelations 2 exceeded expections. The game has been slowed down dramatically and ammo is more scarce, placing an emphasis on survival and the story has been decent, if not a bit Silent Hill like. What I do know was near the end of Barry's level of part two, I was praying that the episode would end soon as I had exhausted almost all of my ammo and herbs and knew that I would not survive another enemy encounter. I've not had this type of anxiety in a game for a long time and it was REFRESHING.

Claire and Barry make a welcomed showing, and brings back references from prior RE's (Jill sandwich). On the other hand, Moira and Natalia are more forgettable, especially their pointing finger/flashlight play mechanic. Apparently Claire and Barry can't see ammo boxes and herbs on shelves right next to them without the the other two pointed them out. I do have more hope for Moira though, as her lines are fairly entertaining sometimes.

Raid mode is where this game really shines, and works almost like a mini Borderlands-esque instance. There are level ups for characters, skills, and weapons and the monsters scale with whatever level your hero is. There are also dailies that provide an extra boost in Exp and money. There is a cash shop but it seems that everything offered in the store can be earned through gameplay (so far). Online co-op has NOT been added yet and that is my main complaint. My other disappointment was the throwback map pack. I was hoping to see remakes of original RE 1, 2, and 3 levels, but it ended up just being rehashes of RE 6 and Revelations 1 maps.

The way this game is going so far I would definitely recommend it. Capcom has priced this game fairly and this is a strong selling point for it.

This is an updated review as of the time of Episode 3. This review primarily focuses on comparing RER1 and RER2.

RER2 got off to a somewhat rocky and "meh" start with the first episode but EP2 and EP3 are significantly better. 

Pros:
+The game mechanics are improved from RER1 and they've maintained the fun stuff from RER1 while adding cool and interesting new stuff like the skill trees. The partner mechanics are fun and allow for plenty of on-the-fly switching during combat for strategy.

+Claire and Barry are back! This might seem like not a big deal but if you are a longtime RE fan it's nice to see them back, and they are handled perfectly.

+Good soundtrack. Not amazing but it is atmospheric and gets the job done. 

+Good replay value for collectibles and medals-- chapters are short, and they're easy to quickly replay to go back and get extras.

+Raid Mode is more fleshed out and is a full-fledged gameplay mode this time, as opposed to it being an afterthought in RER1.


Cons:
-The story has gotten better with EP2-3 but it's really hard to believe they're going to tie all of this up nicely in EP4. 

-Difficulty is a bit average. Especially if you run chapters again to get extras, you will end up with massive stocks of ammo and tons of BP to spend on skill trees, which kind of trivializes the need to bother managing ammo. If you're looking for a challenge, I recommend you play the game straight through once, and don't replay episodes until you've finished the game. 

-No online campaign co-op. This was "acceptable" in RER1 since it was a port of a 3DS game but it just feels like a silly omission here.

-As of this writing there are still some stuttering/freezing issues. I've only ever had the game totally freeze on me once, but the stuttering issues are frequent and irritating. They seem to be working on this so hopefully it will be fully fixed.

This game is a little bittersweet for me. But it also lends hope for the series.
I should start off by saying I really enjoyed RE:REV1. It had, at least for me, good horror, rewarding gameplay, and replayability. Both of the Revelations games are a stark departure from the usual RE formula, and Revelations 2 departs from its predecessor just as much. Returning themes are the gun customizations and BP. That’s ... about it I think. 

I've played through the first two episodes so far and impressions are a little mixed. We'll start with the pros for those without much patience;
- Claire looks like an ACTUAL women. REV1 was mostly you staring at the tight ass of Jill from third person. Fan service, really. But Claire is realistic and I like her much more for that.
- You get about 2 hours of gameplay for 6 bucks. I think that's fine for just one play through.
- If you grew up with this series or played and liked the original REs, there are a few references and fan services for you. Including sandwiches. 
-Scavenging is key. I thoroughly enjoyed the Metro series for it's rewarding scavenging and REV2 usually delivers on that.
- I like the split story telling between the two groups. And each side has their own sort of style of gameplay. Both are potentially fun for me.
- Aside from the film grain, the game looks really good. It's more of a gritty and realistic take. Through, I have preferred to sort of style that RE4 and 5 had graphics wise. 
- I just can't seem to get enough of Barry's voice actor ... or Barry himself for that matter.
-It seems like Revelations is becoming REs proving grounds to experiment. That lends a lot of hope for the atrocity that was RE6. I enjoyed RE6 a lot, actually, but it was a huge let down from RE. If REV2 didn't have the RE name, I would be fooled in to thinking it's an entirely different franchise. It seems to take a lot of inspiration from The Evil Within and even the Metro series. The enemies and settings really remind me of The Evil Within and I'm pretty sure one of the earlier heavy enemies is a subtle reference to Pyramid Head. I hope they go on to maintain a sort of main series and then a sub series in the Revelations' vein. That way if they want to cram as much Quintin Tarentino-y action in to a game as they can like in RE6, the rest of us can still enjoy a sub series. 
- Adding on to the previous point, this game is cheap. Despite having the small price tag, this is a full game. Like I said, this is probably their place to experiment and the lower price tag sends me the message that they understand this isn't meant to a super Triple A game. It's a side story to add on to the series. So with that lower expectation I was left marginally surprised, in a good way.

And now for the cons;
- Killing enemies no longer gives you ammo. This is practically a deal breaker for me. One of the things I loved most about RE4,5, and REV1 was that I could wean ammo from enemies. I liked playing through once with difficulty, then playing through a few more times to grind ammo and just enjoy having that surplus to get my revenge on the harder bosses or enemies. You might sort of do this in Raid Mode but it's just not the same for me.
- There is an incredibly annoying film grain overlay. The Evil Within also had this and I hate it here just as much as I did there. I can't seem to find an option to turn it off, unfortunately. I'm sure they thought this would add to the ambiance but it just becomes distracting. Some may like it and many probably won't notice it as much as I do, though.
- This game acts like a very half assed console port. Enemy path-finding AIs get tripped up, a few graphical bugs, desynced audio on some cutscenes. and unresponsive partners (Very reminiscent of Sheva) really break any immersion you manage to achieve.
- This might be because I'm bad shot and play with a gampad (I usually don't use controllers), but the game can sometimes go beyond hectic and just become unfair or annoying. Ammo never seems to last or be enough. In my experience, I seemed to run out of ammo at the worst possible times. But, again, could just be me. 
- I'm not too sure I like the episodic format. This is just personal taste. On the bright side, if you are very short on cash you can spread the cost of the game out and it does a good job of bringing you back for the next episode. And, you could just wait until all the episodes are out, buy the bundle, and play it all through.

All in all you can only end up wasting 6 bucks if you give the first episode a try. And despite the quirks it has, I've ended up liking it. It's a pretty innocuous investment and if you like it you can get the other episodes when they come out or just wait until they're all out and buy the bundle.

3/5 It's hit or miss, if you restrict yourself to just playing as Moira at every given moment it feels more of a horror survival, gives of an odd RE4 and RE0 like vibe, I liked it better than RE5 and Revelations 1 so take that as you will.

首先，优化的问题的确是存在的，表现于某些时候突然的瞬间顿卡，就是那种突然画面定格然后半秒/一秒后全局瞬移……不过数量不多，可以接受；相比于光影，雾气/颗粒等效果对于帧数的影响要更为明显（比如突击模式里6代雪地那张图）

游戏目前打了两章（目前也就两章Orz）
Ep1的流程比较短，相比较而言Ep2感觉上要长不少；不过从两个章节的流程上来看，克莱尔阿姨这边在游戏性和多样性上都要略逊于巴瑞大叔那边，至少我是这么感觉的——主要原因有二：C&M线的流程变化不够，有点大同小异的感觉，而B&N线这边，敌人变化多不说，娜塔莉这个角色用法上的设定也增加了B&N线的趣味，相比之下那边黑丝妹就有些鸡肋了 = =

这次启示录2有一个优点，恰恰是拜章节式所赐，两条线交叉进行，虽然C&M线多样性比较差，但是和B&N线穿插在一起，节奏上的感觉还是不错的，不像6代4个主线如果选一个一路到底多少会有些审美疲劳。
整体系统，与1代相比，武器与插件系统没有什么实质变化；主要变化在于 1）角色特长：每个角色能干的事情不一样，主要是为双角色服务，体现角色区分度，并且增加合作的必要性（然后卡婊华丽丽地COOP跳票也是醉了……），其中道具搜索也改进了，不是用探测器，而是靠特定角色的能力（和探测器一样，一开始很新鲜，后来就越来越烦了……）　２）角色技能通过评分所得ＢＰ来解锁技能……我不太喜欢在一个所谓的恐怖生存游戏中看到这种设定……不过有就有呗，技能大体上和图集模式中的差不多　３）潜行／暗杀 并不是大多数场景都能依靠潜行灭敌（拜娜塔莉所赐，B&N线机会很多……），不过这个也的确为某些场景提供了另一种选择（不过说实话，多少给人那么些跟风的感觉 ←_← 不过吧6代就已经有类似系统了，

不过说实话你已经卖出那么多DLC的还要氪金的确有些那啥……不得不说学样学得还真快……虽然不影响我们玩游戏但是印象分会大打折扣←_←
（话说拜这次优化所赐，突击模式有两张掉帧神图←_←6代武器店和6代雪地，配置将将达标的筒子遇到这两张图绝对会哭的……

剧情目前不好说……
之前也提过了，C&M线逃啊逃，顺带在顺藤摸瓜；B&N线追寻C&M轨迹。至于这剧情到底好不好，我觉得挺好，虽然还没大量的悬疑来扣住我的心悬，也没有神展开，也没有史诗般地叙事（……），启示录2的故事我感觉，大体上更像是在服务游戏性，配合着游戏场景的切换、玩法的变化……

最后总结下吧：

A long time fan of Resident Evil since the playstation, and even a long time horror fan I have to admit that there are a few gripes with Revelations 2. Since we are in the mood for sandwiches, a la Claire and the infamous Jill sandwich, I'm gonna do a negative sandwich bunned with positives.

It was too early to judge a game by the first episode, but by the second episode it was redeemed. Each episode is about 2 to 4 hours worth of gameplay, which does include both Claires and Barrys paths. Graphics are okay, nothing to much too behold. It is comparable to the graphics of Resident Evil 6. Gameplay is what you would expect from third person shooter and a Resident Evil game, nothing groundbreaking. Each characters non-combatant "co-op" partner provides some skills that compliment the combabatants characters abilities. Moiras flashlight than can blind foes, and Natalias enemy sensing ability.

However, despite having Resident Evil 6 graphics, the game at times does have a slow down of FPS. Most notably in areas with high amounts of effects. It does question why it's happening since the graphics themselves aren't groundbreaking. Speaking of which, a lot of the assets are ripped from Resident Evil 4, 5, and 6; to be more specific the breakable crates and barrels. The inventory system isn't the greatest, nor is it the worst, but it is something. RAID overall is horrible; understanding that it's suppose to be based on an RPG, leveling up and what not, Resident Evil Mercenaries mode is a better alternative. Co-Op in RAID will probably be implemented later, but is not available upon release. There copius amounts of DLC, most of which are extra inventory space for RAID, and alternative costumes for the campaign characters, and characters for RAID(mind you that the characters in RAID are only skins, and have such minor differences that they are not different at all). Episodic releases seems redundant if each episode is going to get released every week.

One of the things that I do enjoy, is that each campaign has a different gameplay aesthetic. Borrowed from Resident Evil 6 on how each campaign plays different, Revelations 2 does the same. Claires campaign is more action oriented, due to enemies being more mobile; whilst in Barrys there are slower, zombie-esque enemies with a touch of enemies similar to those found in Revelations one. The story should not but put aside from only one episode. As a long time fan, the second episode got me hyped for the next release. The general story isn't profound, and employs a past and present narrative. Claires being in the past, and Barrys in the future. While it is cheap to reuse the some of the environments, you do get different scenarios and go to side areas.

In closing, the game is worth the price of $24 or so dollars. From the looks of it, you get about 8-12 hours of gameplay. It is worth buying, right now, or when it's on sale. If you are a long time fan of Resident Evil, and have kept track of the minor details will be rewarded. Heres a hint [spoiler] They didn't forget about Project Wesker and the Wesker children[/spoiler] If you know what I meant, you are in for a treat, if not, well reconsider if you really ARE a fan of Resident Evil since this isn't really explored in the main games,since it was referred only in a small memo. Regardless, it is more of a side story and not really necessary if you don't want to know what has happened to Claire and Barry.

Great atmosphere, engaging characters, excellent voice acting, decent graphics which at times look quite impressive (though probably still not as good as the much older RE5 but that was a much bigger budget release), excellent music and sound effects, decent story, controls generally decent (for an RE game), combat feels very satisfying.

Raid mode is a lot of fun although the difficulty level is more casual than its predecessor which may disappoint some.  At first I was underwhelmed but I came to find it addictive and rewarding. 


Cons: 

Some framerate issues even though I have a powerful i7 system, at times the framerate will dive to the single figures for a few seconds before suddenly going back to a solid 60 (I have it capped at 60 and vsync turned on).  This isn't a frequent or major issue and most of the time the framerate is perfect though. 

Some cutscenes can't be skipped, and those that can sometimes make you wait a few seconds before the skip button will work which is a little thing but it can be annoying. 

The game contains numerous 'cutscene like' moments where you still have control of your character but the game forces you to walk slowly, or snatches the camera view and makes you look somewhere else, which can be jarring and irritating especially in the timed modes. 

Sometimes the partner AI is frustrating, I've had my partner refuse to follow me, and I have to take manual control of them.  Or they walk into danger (such as spinning blades) and get killed.  This isn't a major problem but it could have used a bit of tweaking.

Controls can be a bit fussy at times - you may be standing in front of a lever to pull, or a ladder to climb, and press A to do it, but the game insists you move another few pixels, or sometimes you may have to walk away from it and then back again - these are rough edges which could have been smoothed out.

I didn't expect much from this one, and yet I got much more out of it than from lots of other, far better reviewed games of recent memory.

First of all, the (first episode) of the story campaign is a well done mix of the old and new Resident Evil styles with room for bizarre body horror mutants and slow walking zombies as well. The pacing is really good and fun, violent action as well as slower moments of exploring the creepy hallways both coexist. The game is often surprisingly scary, especially in the second act where you control Barry.

And that's just the first two hours of the game: After that, there's the Raid Mode which turns out to be a completely different game in and of itself. It contains of a bunch of unique levels (not just recycled ones from the single player campaign). You have to shoot your way through them, earn points, purchase new skills and weapons, earn trophies, unlock new levels and then do it all again with another character. It unfolds an incredibly depths and enables a variety of completely different play styles and I'll probably sink many hours into it.

That's what I got for just 6€. It's an incredibly good value for a well produced and polished game (especially the game play). After all the discussions of The Order: 1886 I hope this game might serve as an example of how smaller AAA games can succeed with a more humble pricing and a high focus on gameplay. Resident Evil Revelations 2 has one priority: offering an enjoyable and fun time.

As far as the game goes, it's a satisfying action/horror game. Graphics aren't the best you'll see on pure technical aspect, but there is a style to it, and a good use of lighting, blur and filters. It looks dirty, a bit noisy. The artwork is a step in the good direction after the terrible character design from the first Revelations (I mean, that was god awful...). The enemies aren't the most original, but the protagonists are really well designed, and modeled; they look next-door and at the same time, they have character. The gameplay is more in the steps of Revelations than RE6, which is a good thing. Not that RE6 wasn't good in terms of possibilities (people who REALLY played it knows how much thought went into the mechanics and the overall challenge) but it feels more natural and less super-heroic/block-busterish. And it still gives a great Arcade feel to the Raid Mode which gives the player a way to play the game while waiting for the next episode: nicely done. It's fluid, and the fact that you have to use partner swapping (in story mode) often, is a good addition, though it clearly let that idea go away by the third episode. Overall, I enjoyed the ride, especially for a price so low and that much fun content (the Raid mode is still really enjoyable and that's where I spent most of my time).

BUT...japanese developers don't love the PC too much, do they. The game is weirdly un-optimized. Sometimes, it's fluid 60FPS on highest settings, than BAM 15FPS, and getting to the lower options doesn't help. I had a couple of freeze while trying to load a Raid Mode Lvl too, and the game doesn't feel stable in a general sense. Sometimes, it works perfectly, then you have annoying FPS issues. That's not even talking about the local-coop mode which isn't in the game, but is in the game, but not really, oh but wait you need a mod, but maybe they'll release it with an update.

TL;DR
Fairly good game (I enjoy it much more than the first Revelations, that I already quite liked), with a good money/time ratio (if it's what you are interested in) but poorly executed on PC...

Well, it was pretty good IMO. I won't spoil anything, but I just want to touch upon it. Creepy atmosphere was definitely still there, still prefer Claire and Moira's campaign, as there were much more tense moments. There's a similar scene to RE4 and RE5 where you basically have to hold your ground in a house while enemies are trying to break in. That was great. And in both campaigns you get to meet your first boss fights. Claire's campaign's boss fight is much more dynamic if you will, lots of things going on, granted I am playing on hard difficulty. I don't know how many times I died. Barry's boss fight was more of a rinse and repeat type of thing, at least to me,  it was alright.. But outcome was pretty much the same, I came out of both boss fights with either little ammo (I'm talking like 10 rounds left or less) or none at all with one to no herbs left. That feeling of initial helplessness when you see what you have to overcome with what little you have left is just great, does really bring back old RE memories of resource management. But I did find myself thinking "whhhyyyyy" or "NOOOOooooooooooooo" when I see what I have to face with such little ammunition left, but it's good. That's what survival horror is about. I'm really liking Revelations 2 at the moment. The game isn't completely patched up well yet though, raid mode is definitely still has issues. Campaign for me seems to be working quite well, except for areas where I have to restart b/c I died, I have stuttering and fps issues for the first 30 seconds or so. I'm writing this review soley based on the game itself, not based on the PC co-op blunder, because honestly I feel like not enough people are giving credit to where it's due, and also, I'm not that big on co-op either in the main story, but I would definitely like to see co-op in raid mode. 

Anyway, on to the review.

So far, Revelations 2 has a great atmosphere. Pretty creepy at times, and it does definitely bring back memories of old RE titles because there are areas of back tracking, such a refreshment from the linear RE6 campaign. Revelations 2 plays a bit like The Last of Us, which is a good thing. I love the new implementation of being able to crouch. And the afflicted that come running at you is pretty nerve racking, which is similar to the runners in TLoU. Also similar to TLoU is the crafting system, although not as robust, but just reminded me of it. The ability to swap characters anytime you wish is something I really like too, more so in Claire and Moira's campaign than Barry's, but nonetheless, I'm liking this new gameplay addition. Does certainly give the player more freedom.   I am also quite fond of the new dodge mechanic. Much better than the dodge mechanic from the first revelations, and isn't over the top like in RE6  (jumping to the side and rolling and getting up again). I do feel like Revelations 2 strikes a nice balance in terms of being not too action-y and not too tank control like. However, I would like slightly tighter controls during sprinting. One thing I LOVE is that enemies do not have health or ammo drops. YES. This is what I'm talking about. I legitimately was running out of ammo on my play through as Claire (hard difficulty) and it was glorious. Me likey. Production value is definitely up from the first Revelations title, but still a step away from the main AAA RE installments, but it still looks and feels great. However, I wish that there were more melee options. If only it had RE5's melee gameplay, where there's different melee animations depending on how the enemy is staggered.
So far, I am impressed with the first episode, hopefully, I will continue to be with the other subsequent episodes to come. I just hope the story doesn't turn out to be some crazy plot like Revelations 1...

Raid Mode
If you were like I, and wasn't much fond of Raid Mode in Revelations 1, I think you'll really like this new Raid Mode in Revelations 2. Now it doesn't seem like a chore to play. Matches are just right in length, much more customization options to make you come back for more. It seems like the roster is going to be quite robust. It would be nice if pretty much all the RE characters were to be included. We already know Leon, Chris will be. I'm hoping for at least Sherry, Ada, Rebecca, and Jessica. They have to include Sherry because Claire is there...wouldn't it be nice?

Cons
-Bug, bugs everywhere! Campaign seems to be alright, for the most part. but there are instances of really bad stuttering and frame rate drops, and lip sync issues (most notably the first real time cutscene in Barry's campaign). After the first patch, it has gotten slightly better for me, but definitely still there. I am running an i7-3770K, 16GB ram, R9 290, and I get areas of 30~ish fps especially when there are effects on the screen (snow, fire, hard lighting). Most I've seen come from raid mode, possibly because of the variations in environment/stages that bring these issues up. 
-Slow mo. I feel like my character seems to be running in slow mo at times, especially during reloads animations. I'm not sure if it's due to the stuttering/fps issue.
-When aiming, sometimes the thing that you're aiming at is slightly out of focus, and also the laser sight as well. Other times it's fine. Also not liking how the character is also out of focus/slightly fuzzy when aiming as well. Really reminds me of RE6 when it first came out too. If they fixed it for RE6, why implement it in Revelations 2?
-Enemy AI can be really stupid sometimes. They can get stuck in doorways or window sills or run in circles trying to get to you on another level but have no idea that the stairs is just behind them (experienced in raid mode). Had an enemy just turn around and walk into those spinning spike traps during the campaign when Claire was at the door way, crouched and slightly out of view from it. It kept on walking into the wall next to the door way, gave up and committed suicide. 

Even with these cons, it doesn't render the game unplayable. Yes, I know there's those out there where the bugs do render the game unplayable for them, and that's quite unfortunate. But for me, it's just something I'll have to live with until a patch comes out that fixes everything, which I'm pretty confident that Capcom will do, since the first patch rolled out two days after release. However, it does leave a sour taste in one's mouth, especially for PC gamers when the game is not properly ported/optimized.

I honestly wasn't expecting much out of Revelations 2, after Resident Evil 6 and the original Revelations, the latter of which I personally felt was not the "return to form" that many claimed it to be. That said, Revelations 2 was quite the surprise. The closest in the series I can compare it to is RE5's "Lost in Nightmare" DLC, both in the way they control and the way they focus more on exploration, a little stealth and ammo management over the straight, action-heavy gameplay of RE5 and RE6.

I suppose the highest praise I can give Revelations 2 is that, in certain aspects, it reminded me a lot of the much-loved Outbreak titles. Even if you're a not a huge fan of the series, or an old fan that didn't care for the past few titles, there's a little bit of something for everyone in Revelations 2.

*I can't really speak to the overall story just yet, thanks to Capcom's ridiculous decision to split the game into 4 pieces, making this an episodic release.

Before I carry on with the review, let me post my computer's specifications:

i7 4770k @ 4.5 Ghz
GTX 780 x 2 (SLI)
32Gb Corsair Vengeance @ 1866Mhz
500Gb Samsung 840 Evo (SSD)
1Tb HDD

I've had EVGA Precision X track the framerate, GPU usage, and VRAM usage for this game.  I never saw RER2 use more than 1Gb of VRAM... not even with ever setting set as high as it could go with the FXAAHQ3; hell, I even enabled 8 CSAA in nVidia's control panel (didn't really need to).  My system never used more than 1Gb of VRAM and GPU usage stayed under 40% for each card.

With my beefy system I still encountered massive framerate drops (as low as 20fps) without any corresponding spike in VRAM/GPU usage... no CPU bottleneck either.  Lowering the settings does not yield a descernible benefit or increase in fps.

I love Resident Evil especially the ingegration of coop in the more recent games. Im happy that Capcom has added local coop to PC but would love to see online coop as well. As far as gameplay goes they've come a long way in removing some of the clunky mechanics as well as keeping the action tense. The atmoshpere is great and the graphics are great. Basically if you love Resident Evil or survival horror you will most likely love this game.

Though at the first week of this game's launch, it has many drawbacks, the latest patches solved most of the microstuttering issues I've experienced before. With the new patches, the game runs smoothly at the maximum settings on 1080p with 60 constant FPS. That was great. 

The story is good and so far, interesting enough to immerse me with the plot's elements. The mystery, the characters, and the events make the game far more immersive than I have expected. Although, not all games make me feel this way, this game is by far one which made that possible. That was another great factor to recommend this game.

The graphics as well as the gameplay are great. Challenging enough to make me try the game for a few times. The replayability? Oh well, it is well-hyped for me. I think I'll play this game with a partner next time, in splitscreen mode. The enemies, zombies, and other enemy types are also challenging that my character died a few times before I was able to beat them (especially the big zombie who throws fire at Claire and Moira on episode 2). The ammunition, green leaves, red leaves, and other items are scarce that makes this game more difficult to beat even at normal difficulty.

Last but not the least, I'll discuss about the negative side of this game. First is the game support: CAPCOM's support was very unresponsive and awful because they don't try to at least control the situation by just simply communicating with their customers, especially the ones who are still experiencing bugs and issues within the game. How can another customer buy another one of their games if their support staff is as lousy as this? Come on CAPCOM, just give your people some reassurances so that they can also give their faith in your company, especially to your staff. I'm not reviewing for your company though, I'm reviewing for your game but I'll write this to at least put you back to your senses. Lastly, although the graphical and the stuttering issues had been fixed (in most PC depending upon the specifications), the issue about the game crashing whenever I try to access the status screen in the campaign is still unfixed by any patch released by CAPCOM. I was able to fix this by moving the installation directory of the game from my D drive to the original steamapps folder in my C drive, and voila, the bug was gone which means that this can only be fixed through the user's/customer's end and not through CAPCOM support. This solution was suggested by a user at the steam forums. The weird thing though was that when I've tried to play the pirated version of this game and it was installed in my D drive, this issue does not exist at all, only in the original steam version. There might be some errors within the codes of the patch sent by CAPCOM devs as the pirated version I had installed had no patches within it. Well, the problem was solved so this won't be an issue for good.

Final verdict: The story, the graphics, and the gameplay are all astonishing, not to mention the aspect of having the raid mode, it makes the game more enjoyable and more worthwhile to have. Neglecting the poor support from CAPCOM, I'll give this game a grade of 9/10.

I have only recently played through various Resident Evil Games over the last couple of years including the first Revelations. This game is released with a four episode campaign with episodes released at different dates. This allows you to follow the story over time like a Telltale game. However, there is a bit more action involved here. There are four characters you control in all, two sets of two. Barry and Natalia, Rachel and Moira. All characters need to be used to complete episodes. Moira and Natalia have unique abilities that you use to get past certain obstacles. The graphics are quite nice and although you move along a mostly linear path, there are secrets and items scattered around to find, increasing the re-playability. You also have difficulty modes and an invisible and countdown mode for each episode. The story fits nicely into the Resident Evil universe and you will care about the characters on their journey. 

There is an additonal RAID mode that allows you to fight infected of different types and levels. This is where the game should shine. However, at the time of writing there were a few issues with this:

1) I have to play in offline mode, as a soon as it tries to connect to server it freezes or crashes. This is workable, but hopefully it will be fixed at some point soon.
2) There is currently no online multiplayer, when added the experience will be twice as good.
3) A split screen mode was promised and then removed at last minute. However, they have promised to look into this and offer something to compensate (no idea what at the moment).

Basically this is a great game for fans of the Resident Evil universe and there is a lot to keep you interested. You might want to wait until they fix the RAID mode before getting it though.

I got this game with minimal expectations, yet Capcom still very nearly managed to disappoint me. This game on release was, without a doubt, just not properly play-tested for the PC. [b]Edit patch 2.1:[/b] The performance issues have been fixed. Thank you, Capcom.

[h1][b]Cons:[/b][/h1]
[strike][h1]Poor graphics performance[/h1][/strike]
[b]Edit Patch 2.1:[/b] Fixed, but I gather some people still suffer frame stutter.

[h1]Odd surround audio[/h1]
I often hear sounds coming from right beside me. Actually the foe giggling maniacally is indeed right beside me, just a floor up.

[h1]Wonky keyboard + mouse controls[/h1]
Very wonky. I've got a controller, but I prefer keyboard and mouse. Often the camera tilts in the exact opposite direction to my mouse movements, presumably because it's expecting the motion of an analog stick.

[h1]Terribly-tested Gameplay[/h1]
Rewards (both Campaign and Raid) place a lot of emphasis on takedowns, yet there's a snag. 

As you come out of a finisher, you are instantly vulnerable. It's annoying, because the camera angles so you can't see much during the kill, and leaves you completely unprepared. Coming out of it I wish there'd be a reprieve, like momentary invulnerability. This is just a quirk I have, so feel free to dismiss it.

Mouseclicks are interchangeable with the pick up and climb keys for... some... reason. So if there happens to be a ledge or ammo nearby, be prepared to see your character climb up a ledge or vault instead of performing a finisher/melee to conserve ammo.

Raid Mode: [spoiler]The unlockable character Cipher was extremely poorly-thought out. It seems Capcom's thought process did not go beyond, "Hey, let's give him a katana. That'll be cool". A lot of the enemies explode, Capcom. Even before unlocking his weapon slot at level 8.[/spoiler]

Hunk's Stealth skill looks to be bugged. There are times when a Revenant was still able to track me under cloak. It seems to be an AI issue, since the same happens with a decoy bottle, but it's a nice way to muck up a DLC character right off the bat. You should've tested this thoroughly, Capcom.

Campaign: [b]Episode 3:[/b][spoiler]If you progress through the opening tear-jerker piggyback scene of Barry's episode too quickly, and they haven't read all their lines, the game will crash. :D[/spoiler]

I am absolutely convinced they did not do [i]any[/i] playtesting on release.

[h1]Fairly awful Raid Mode UI[/h1]
Objective markers will overlay anything, so you've got a giant icon hovering over the middle of your screen. 

[b]Edit patch 2.2:[/b] They've made an attempt at moving item icons to the side, which is a start. No idea why all the other UI elements (like the exit icon) are still completely opaque. Try shooting anything when half your screen is filled with "Elite" icons.

On top of that, Raid Mode [b]definitely[/b] feels unfinished. None of the missions have level descriptions/pictures to jog your memory; just a one-line objective. You're stuck memorizing which mission number corresponds to which arena.

[h1]Online Store/DLC:[/h1]
The folks at Capcom are releasing additional... weapon space? For a price. 

I understand that there ought to be a limit on the number of weapons/parts, but paying for more storage is an odd way to conduct business. I think somewhere down the line Capcom thought RE turned into an MMO or something.

[strike][h1]No Co-Op[/h1]
[b]Edit patch 1.3:[/b] Capcom had in the past hinted at online Co-op, and has integrated the beta offline co-op patch with the public release.[/strike]

[b]Edit patch 3.0:[/b] Raid Mode now has online co-op support, but you're in for long waits. Luckily, you can invite friends who own the game.

[h1]Leveling system in raid mode[/h1]
You'll only unlock all four weapon slots at higher levels, meaning you're restricted to one or two firearms until you unlock the other slots. This messes up my innate weapon-mapping. So instead of thinking that I've got my shotgun bound to a certain key, I now have to remember weapon-bindings for each and every character in Raid Mode.

It looks like this was an attempt at balancing characters' strengths, but there are better ways.


[h1][b]Pros:[/b][/h1]
[h1]Story[/h1]
... doesn't disappoint. There are very witty jabs that tie into RE/Biohazard history. And frankly, the scripts in the RE universe are not known for wit.

I was genuinely creeped out by the endgame boss, and despite each being a single episode-long, the bonus episodes were very well done.

[h1]Characters[/h1]
I'm a huge fan of this franchise, and I half-expected that Capcom botched up Moira to be yet another token throwaway character, or one that swears every five seconds. She still cusses, but her personality is likeable and there are some strong attempts at character development throughout the main campaign and bonus episodes.

[h1]Atmosphere[/h1]
I went into this game thinking that I shouldn't expect a resurgence of "old school" survival horror, that those days were long past. Yet this game does do a good job of reliving the "feel", I guess. It isn't true Survival Horror where you attempt to run by foes, and avoid fights as much as possible, but there is a pleasing homage to it.

There are definite attempts to utilize stealth and environmental hazards to minimize ammo usage. A key mechanic throughout the game requires you to focus and scavenge items you'd otherwise miss.

[h1]Inventory Management: So long as you're not cut off, both characters can freely combine across each other's packs[/h1]
The powers that be have decided to be very merciful. There is limited space and an abundance of everything, so it helps that you can combine items even if the components are on different characters.

[h1]No QTEs, at least those like in RE6[/h1]
Same as the first RE:Revelations. ThankyouThankyouThankyou.

[h1]Offline play[/h1]
Not sure if this counts as a "pro", or simply "not a con", but an active network connection is not required to play Raid Mode. My internet was fine, but an in-game notification stating "network connection was lost" paused my game, and I feared the worst. Luckily, the game still allows you to play on after dismissing the warning. Aw, Capcom, you're so considerate (Now please stop charging for extra parts' space).

[list]
[*]Basic Movement is done with WASD, Camera is on free look and controlled by mouse, but character will always stand face forward/back to the camera like in RE:Rev, character will always run and sprinting is same as in RE6.
[*]Dodging is similar to RE:Rev "dash to direction while duck under the attack", but is now usable anytime with dodge button and direction button, like in RE6. Dodging is not full dodge, timing is still important and direction you dodge, since some monster attacks can't be dodged with certain directions.
[*]Weapon usage is still same as in first Revelations, same goes for upgrades. No Secondary firing mechanism.
[*]RE:Rev2 has Skill upgrades and BPs (Bonus Points) are used as currency to unlock and improve abilities (Same points are also used to unlock extra content, like concept art and figurines). [/list]

Even then, characters weren't acting like they were straight out of Lethal Weapon, Die Hard or some other ish. They constantly (and I do mean constantly) crack wise about their circumstances, spouting horrible one liners and psuedo-badass quips every few feet. This might not have been THAT bad if the story didn't try to make you take it seriously. They'll act one way in in cutscenes, then in-game act the complete opposite. I feel there's no real consistency to any of them. There's one point where one particular character receives what should be devastating news, soul crushing stuff and they don't even really react accordingly. -Enemy design I found to be really bland, save for the final boss, who looked truly disturbing.

RER2 is a terrible port. It's poorly optimized to the extent that I doubt the "minimum requirements" are truly enough to run it, and the coop doesn't work. HOWEVER, as a game, RER2 is everything I wanted it to be. Hell, it's everything I wanted Resident Evil 5 & 6 to be; genuinely atmospheric in single-player, with companions that don't waste ammo by default and who won't need you to save them every ten seconds. I've yet to encounter any QTE sections, and as I only play keyboard this is a huge plus. I even like that you can switch between your useful (carries gun) and not-so useful (uses melee weapon/carries flashlight/fits in tight spaces) characters at will, and that anyone who plays single-player is forced to do so if you want to find half the ammo in a level. For the first time in a Resident Evil game I found myself genuinely desperate for more bullets, and it's actually kinda fun (anyone who struggled to keep enough ammo in RE4 may have less fun).

Raid mode, the thing you do after you beat story mode, has been giving some people problems. However, aside from the occasional frame drop, I've found Raid mode to be a highly playable variation on the hoard mode formula. You'll encounter specialized/modified monsters, unlock weapons, and earn cash and experience to put toward a character upgrade system (there's a similar skill system in single-player, but there doesn't seem to be any overlap between the two). 

RAID MODE FEATURES MICROTRANSACTIONS, but the things you can buy appear to be mostly meaningless: gems that allow you to continue a Raid mission without losing any found items or progress, and extra guns and parts. RAID MODE LOCKS ELEMENTS OF GUN/UPGRADE STORAGE AS DLC, which is sad, but you are free to sell any weapons/upgrades you don't want/need.

Does releasing a bad port and sticking in microtransactions make Capcom a huge corporate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥? Yes. Do I regret my purchase? Not at all.

Buy if you like Resident Evil.

This is a fun resident evil so I would recommend it, especially at it's low price, but it's not a great, cannonical-style resident evil.  It doesn't feel completely 100% console, it feels a bit like a handheld game.  It's fairly low-poly, the environments aren't as cool as many resident evils, and it's got forced NPC characters that accompany you completely along the way (something people complained about in RE5).  These forced NPCs don't really add much to the game, they have the ability to see things in the environments that the "main" character can't, so instead of looking forward to using a different character, I felt obliged to do so just to find items in my environment, even if that's not really the case.  I understand why capcom did this though.  This is a series that was once criticized for keeping very similar gameplay for a long time and not "innovating", something that Capcom has obviously taken to heart.  

So, these things do keep this from being a great resident evil, but it's definitely not bad.  It's still classic, fun, cheesy resident evil gameplay, and if you're a RE fan, there's nothing wrong with that.  It feels a lot like the first revelations, and overall, it's worth the price they're asking for it.  If you're one of those people who are seriously going to throw a hissy-fit over them forgetting to mention that there's currently not local split-screen co-op on this $6 game, don't buy it.  Instead go back to doing whatever it is that makes you happy(obviously complaining).  I give it a 7/10.

So there has been a lot of negativity surrounding this game, mostly due to the lack of "co-op" that was mentioned on the Steam store page prior to launch, so let me throw my hat into the ring;

First of all; Capcom have apologised due to any misunderstandings caused by the way the game was listed on Steam, The have also stated that they are looking into ways of re-implementing the missing split-screen mode.

With that said, the only co-op in the original Revelations was raid mode, and that game is, and has always been, listed as having 'co-op' on it's Steam store page - I have no idea why some people expected there to be online campaign co-op in Revelations 2 or are annoyed that it doesn't exist. [b]This was never intended, or mentioned, at -any point- during the game's development or the build up to release.[/b]

I'd also like to point out that, as mentioned by Capcom (and as was always intended) "Raid mode will support online co-op shortly after launch when a free patch is available for players to download which adds this feature" - So technically, just like the original Revelations, the game will have a co-op feature. There's no 'scam' or 'false advertising' like some of the wild claims other people have been making; This is how the game was intended to be. If you thought differently, you should have done your homework (or played the first Resident Evil Revelations, which would have told you exactly how co-op in this game was going to work).

With that addressed, I'll move on to the actual game itself:

Having completed the the first episode of the story, I can say that, so far, the atmosphere is fantastic. The way the game is being released episodically isn't a bad thing, instead of burning through the game in just a couple of days, like a favourite TV series, you have to wait to find out what happens, which aids in building the suspense factor nicely. Can't wait for next week.

The characters feel like they have been properly worked on rather than just 'copy paste name from RE game here'. I was super excited as a long time RE fan to finally see Barry Burton back, and for the first time (not including that awful gameboy outing) as a playable character, I can say that I'm not disappointed. The scripting and voice acting work is great and goes a long way to making the characters feel 'real' - Moira in particular acts just like you'd expect your typical teenager to.

Gameplay is solid. The two-character system is a fantastic feature, instead of just having an AI partner following you around, getting to instantly switch between and fully use both characters is brilliant and helps in just about every situation in the game. Raid mode is fun, and feels like a combination of both old and new "Mercenaries" modes, time attack style gameplay, but with a goal and the ability to kill all enemies in the stage.

Graphically the game looks nice, the character models in particular are very nicely detailed and the environments do their jobs well. Like some other people, I had some performance issues until I tweaked the settings and capped the frame rate, it doesn't run brilliantly by any means, but I wasn't expecting it to on my now outdated 560ti, (I imagine it will run a little better after a couple of patches and a game-ready graphics driver.) No game-breaking bugs or crashing, nothing major on that front.

The micro-transactions in raid mode aren't anything I would spend my money on, though it seems like all of the stuff in there is completely unnecessary (extra continues should you run out; I've not used a single one yet, extra item storage, items you can get just by playing for the ultra-lazy). It kind of feels like an obvious cash grab attempt and in my opinion, the game would be better off without it... That said, it can be completely ignored and doesn't detract from the gameplay in any way, so it's not a big deal.

So far, my considered opinion, I'd give this a solid 7/10, stand out point being one of the few games recently that has instantly grabbed my attention and made me care about the story, biggest negatives being the sub-optimal performance and those annoying micro-transactions.

If you're a fan of Resident Evil, the campaign makes it worth getting now, if you're not that interested in the series and are looking at it from the point of view as it just being a game to play, I'd say stick it on your wish list and wait for the next sale.

A preliminary review based on current observations from Episodes 1 and 2 can be found below. 

The good:

[h1](+)[/h1] Perhaps this game's most innovative aspect is [b]revisitation[/b]. You fight your way with Clair and Moira through one place, and then Barry and Natalia show up in the same place later. Whichever way you affect the environment with the first duo, the second will be there to witness it (or fight it). It makes you plan ahead and think twice as hard for both pairs of characters. 

[h1](+)[/h1] Many of its qualities so far, from the almost intentionally [b]so-bad-it's-good dialogue[/b] and golden continuity nods, to the airtight [b]resource management[/b] and neatly hidden objects, feel like a true service to the fans of survival horror genre, and classical RE games specifically. 

[h1](+)[/h1] It combines those properties with [b]smooth character animations[/b], mildly [b]challenging gameplay[/b], and the first Revelations' simple yet satisfying [b]customization system[/b]. The more valuable a weapon part is, the harder it's gonna be to obtain. 

Edit: I take that "mildly" back. Enemies in Episode 2 are far more challenging.

[h1](+)[/h1] The new [b]talent tree[/b] they've added lends you specific secondary abilities that you can do without if you so please, but they can certainly help a lot, especially ones that have to do with healing or dealing damage. It's more of a flavor addition than a mandatory component.

[h1](+)[/h1] Raid mode, like "Mercenaries" mode in other REs, adds to the very much needed [b]replay value[/b] that a lot of other games today seem to neglect. Raid mode has strong RPG elements, like leveling up, which grants access to skills, equipping a set of passive skills and weapons, and a plethora of different activities to play.

The bad:

[h1](-)[/h1] A few [b]enemy animations[/b] are unpleasant to look at and seem almost amateurishly done, especially the faster ones.

[h1](-)[/h1] I would normally forgive bad dialogue from Capcom games in general, but no one says "what in a moist barrel of ♥♥♥♥♥" or "mother of balls" in a life-threatening situation. Not that I object to profanity, in fact I relish in it, but some of the curse words they've used seem so artificial and unspontaneous. 

[h1](-)[/h1] Having to unlock a certain ability using BP (Battle Points) before you could have your armed [b]partner assist[/b] you in combat is not a good idea, though the fact that he/she won't spend any ammo by doing so kind of balances it out. 

Edit: Even with the partner assist skill unlocked, it seems your armed partner will shoot so scarcely and so infrequently that you're better off assuming direct control of them and doing the shooting yourself.

[h1](-)[/h1] There are [b]two different "pick-up" buttons[/b], one for files and one for equipment, which I find entirely unnecessary and confusing.

[h1](-)[/h1] Seeing my mouse cursor during cutscenes is a big no-no.

[h1](-)[/h1] The whole thing in general, to me, [b]feels low budget[/b]. It could be argued that this is because of the aforementioned few bad enemy animations, but I personally can't put my finger on why it feels so.

Now what?

[h1](%)[/h1] As of Episode 2, things are certainly looking up. The second episode is a massive improvement; the plot is taking turn for the better, enemies are getting much more challenging, and plenty more secret areas to explore.

[h1](%)[/h1] Even with the game's flaws, it is certainly unfair to brush it off as bad. The two episodes we have right now consistently prove that this game has a lot to offer.

[h1](%)[/h1] If you enjoy third person shooters, have enjoyed some of the older RE games, or are generally a fan of the survival horror genre, I can confidently say this game will appeal to you.

- Microtransactions:  Want extra storage space for your raid mode gear?  That'll be $1.99.  This isn't an MMO, save files are stored locally so there is no reason for this.  This is just a cheap cash grab attempt.

Overall the core gameplay experience of both Story and Raid mode are solid. [h1]Overview[/h1]
Whatever your opinion of this whole PC same-screen co-op “scandal”, as some people say, the game itself is still fun to play. It’s Resident Evil, and comes with all the quirks and issues that have plagued the other titles, but is still a fun game to play.

[h1]Story/Atmosphere[/h1]
As only one episode has been released, the story is still somewhat unknown. The events of episode one take place many years after those of the original game. You begin as Claire, waking up in a prison cell, with no clue as to where you are or how you got there. You soon meet up with Moira, Barry’s daughter, and adventure together. You do eventually leave the prison itself, only to discover where you are.

The second part of episode one has you playing as Barry, who received a distress call from Moira, and has come to the prison to investigate (how he tracked the location down we’ll either find out later, or may never know). He meets a young girl named Natalie, who winds up accompanying him in his search, because why not take a little girl into a monster infested location while you search for your daughter who sent out a distress call from a monster infested location.

The story isn’t too convoluted, yet, but that will surely change. Capcom is known for throwing twists and turns at every corner.
Once you find out where you are, you’ll come to appreciate the location. Capcom has done a great job rendering the prison and its surroundings, and you’ll get to see many parts of it, from both Claire and Barry’s perspective.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Gameplay is almost similar to the Outbreak games, where you control multiple people. As Claire, you’ll be accompanied by Moria, who holds a flashlight while you hold the gun. Why Claire is incapable of holding both a gun and a flashlight I don’t know, but that would throw off the whole mechanics of the game, I guess. After a certain point, you can freely switch between both characters, and you will need to do that for certain parts of the story. Moira can also find collectibles, or ammo, or other items by seeing a glint, then shining the light at the glint to make it interactive, allowing her (or Claire) to pick it up. If the AI is controlling Moira, you can’t do this.

The same goes for Barry and Natalie. Natalie can crawl through small spaces to open the way for Barry, while also being able to point at glinting objects (literally, you point), which allows her or Barry to then pick up that object.

Like the first Revelations, you can dodge enemy attacks, but the dodge seems far superior and actually works, compared to the first game. You have the quick turn (180), and can walk while firing.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
The game looks good. Characters are well detailed, except for their faces. Claire quite often looks like she’s constipated. Environments are dark, disturbing, moody, dank, etc. I find the enemy models to be terrific.

The environment is done well, too. Trees cast an eerie glow from the sky, bushes and leaves rustle. Is it your AI partner running through that bush, or something else?

There isn’t a lot of graphical options to set in-game, and are pretty much standard fare.

And while the game does look good, it doesn’t look fantastic. But, such is life when it comes to what is essentially a straight port. Resident Evil games have always been developed with a console first attitude, and that’s fine. But Capcom is especially lazy and/or incompetent when it comes to porting games. Resident Evil HD Remaster is the exception to this rule, and is actually a very well done port.

[h1]Sound/Music[/h1]
The music, as usual for Resident Evil games, is great. If you pre-ordered it, you get some soundtrack selections. My game only has four music files, but I don’t know if more will be released with each episode, or if that is the extent of it.

Sound effects are great, and really lead to some tense moments. The acting, while passable, is like all Resident Evil games, and occasionally sounds forced while always sounding cheesy. The characters even poke fun at certain things, such as Claire exclaiming how she didn’t become a Claire sandwich, and Barry making fun of his master of unlocking comment from 1996.

[h1]Performance[/h1]
And this is where Resident Evil Revelations 2 falters. The performance is spotty. Often times, when readying your gun to aim, there’s some slight lag as the game zooms in to your character’s head. There are lots of moments where the framerate stutters for no apparent reason. It’s a completely unoptimized product. Which is also evident when the game tells you not to turn off your console while its saving. Yes, the PC version tells you not to shut off your CONSOLE. If that isn’t incompetent “optimizing”, I don’t know what is.

I didn’t experience any crashes or startup issues.

[h1]Multiplayer Info[/h1]
So this is what’s causing an uproar by a lot of fans. The PC version of Revelations 2 is the only version not to have local, offline co-op. Not that it’ll be patched in later, but it just doesn’t have it to begin with. I don’t get the big deal myself, but I can understand how people feel deceived by Capcom, as this information was not originally in the game description, so people who pre-ordered or bought it thinking they’d be able to play locally with a friend are annoyed, and for good reason.

Online co-op for Raid mode (not the campaign) is to come in a later patch. If I remember, I’ll update my review accordingly whenever that happens.

[h1]Everything Else[/h1]
The game is short. I completed both acts of the first episode in about three hours. Let’s assume each episode is about that time, you’re looking at twelve hours of a story once all episodes are out (four episodes at three hours each). It’s not horrible that it’s short, and it’s not a full priced game either, so value for money is pretty on par.

Raid mode, while fun, is somewhat boring at the moment, as you’re limited to playing yourself. Once co-op is patched in, I’m sure it’ll get better.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
Don't judge the game based on Capcom's multiplayer issue. Judge the game on what it is; a game. Don't give it a bad review because you're ticked off with them, give it a bad review if it's actually a bad game.

It’s Resident Evil, and you either love or hate them. I, personally, have hated the fact that the games have taken an action-heavy stance, and I loved the slow and methodical pace of the first three games. However, it’s still a fun title, with what little time you’ll need to invest into it. And the story is always worth seeing.

Also, Barry. Barry is back.

Review after finishing episode 1/4::
The game ran smooth for me at 60fps (locked) and only dropped when autosaves occured and I really enjoyed it. Sure it's short but no longer than a Telltale episode and their is much more "playing" involved here.
While the game is truly picking up it's mechanics from the RE4+ series of games it seems to have dialled back on the whole massive set pieces that RE fans hated about the 6th game. Looking foward to Episode 2.

Review after finishing episode 2/4:
Ep2 significally ups the ante in both characters sections, with some meaty story hooks and a new more open map in one section akin to the village from RE4 or Evil Within and a pretty good character/boss fight that gets some satisfying development and back story. After episode 2 I am enjoying where the story is leading and the dynamic between the games main characters as well as it's secondary characters.

Review ater finishing episode 3/4:
Claires campaign is the one that shines in this episode as we learn more backstory to the characters and especially Moira herself. The episode mixes some good story telling with a lot simplistic puzzles which brings a certaint something back that old school Resident Evil fans will have missed. Some of the action sequences in this episode certainly throw Claire and Moira through the grill but it's worth it to experience the end of Claires segment which is the best the game has been so far. Barry's section on the other hand kind of gets a little less love this time around. While there are some touching moments in this episode for Barry, it's let down by the fact that half of it is just carrying a big box around. Still, the episode overall is great and the game continues to impress.

Review ater finishing episode 4/4:
Claires Campaign takes the sideline this time around with it clocking in around 20 mins and only having any story development at the very start and very end, good but nothing that they couldn't have added at the end of the last episode for Claire. Barry on the other hand brings his A game this time around with his section lasting around 2 1/2 hours on my playthrough. Barrys section features a couple of puzzles and a good variety in locations with the pinnacle being a throwback to Resident Evil 1 near the end. The climax has some good ideas in terms of trying to change up the stale boss fight formula and gives Barry one of the greatest moments in the whole game. A satisfying end to an overall good package. 

The 2 bonus episodes also reveal a couple of things from the main campaign that aren't explained so to get the overall story playing these is recommended.

As many avid fans of Resident Evil will tell you; before you read on, curb your enthuiasm and leave it at the door because 'This game contains scenes of explicit gobshite and poor quality.'

By now, the Resident Evil franchise is becoming a fossilised shadow of its former self and is desperately trying to recapture the essence of its glory days with all of the budgeting and none of its soul and that is exactly what it feels like, a budget rendition of the far more successfully acclaimed Resident Evil: Revelations which was a remarkable step in the right direction; but as they say, one step forward and two steps back.

RE:R2 is in some dire trouble right out of the gate for as soon as you boot the game up, you are whisked into watching the opening cutscenes in forced 720x480 quality. No time for the main menu then? I suppose you want this ♥♥♥♥ over as fast as possible? Fair enough given the drunken state you are in, Capcom.
An immediate escape as soon as I have skipped the cutscenes and I am on the main menu, sorting out what I assumed at the time was just a small misfire on its own part, no big deal but as soon as I am back in the game restarting; more warning bells begin to kick in, the screen tearing is real but what becomes worse is the absolute diabolical level of voice acting and audio work, a party thrown in the honour of TerraSave, that feels completely devoid of life and any enthusiasm, quiping awful lines of dialogue such as "terr... doesn't have to end with ...rist" .... What.. Resident Evil was founded on cheesy dialogue but it had a sense of class and elegance beneathe the full plates of cheese, it was down right campy and we loved it for that but then, enter Claire Redfield.

Addressing the fan-boyism so we can move past this, I just want to say; Alyson Court (The true 'Voice' of Claire Redfield) I am so, so sorry for the complete butchering of a character you made your own, one that you have dedicated your voice talent, heart and soul, to bring to so many gamers over the span of the last eighteen years.
Claire Redifeld, now, has no passion, no character and no interest in her own voice work to even be compared. This voice actress sounds how wet cardboard looks and is completely devoid of emotion, taking the term 'B-Movie' to new lows.

On the opposite end of the spectrum however, is the newly introduced, Moira Burton and daughter of "What IS this?" Barry Burton. Two individual voice actors who have all the spark and interest of wanting to get involved with the franchises colourful past and give it their all. Barry & Moira are both well written, brash, spunky, relatable and moreover, an interesting pair of characters to want to get to know. Of the current roster, Moira & Barry Burton are the most grounded and well realised of the plot so far.

EPISODE 1:
The presentation and graphics, though appearing dated by todays standards, hold up well once you are in the game and you take control of the characters. Animations are fluid for the most part such as when your character takes heavy damage, they do become visibly more stressed and tired as they will hunch over and clamber for dear life, using a tourniquet if they begin to bleedout all over the screen will ensure survival just long enough for you to see the next green herb, lip syncing however is one major factor that is so HORRIBLY off, they may as well be 5000 yards from one another and hearing distant echos long after the talking stops, much like radio signals travelling through our cosmos. 

The detail of the environments is just the right level of grimey without becoming imposing or vulgar. Environments are generally well rendered, appropriately dim and equally unnerving, allowing RE fans to settle right in based solely on the visual aesthetics that have come to be expected of a Resident Evil title. It begins typically linear as you move through tight, narrow hallways filled with prison cells, medical bays, antiseptic batheing rooms and large trash compactors full of large insects and all kinds of nasty; with some bewildering environmental traps, it is clear to see that architect George Trevor, has had an obvious admirer here at the prison, which clearly is not a redressed Rockfort Island (anyone?). Once the Prison opens up to some exterior locations, the quality in presentation jumps up higher as light shafts and dynamic looking fog set in that gives the environment itself some real character. It is beautiful, mysterious and has a few vistas to really breathe in and appreciate. The simulacrum of a sprawling Island is a gorgeous thing to behold, even if the grass tends to wave a little preternatural.

The story moves at a rather steady pace based on higher difficulties although I wished your antagonists would have done the same as many of those enemies you will fight appear to be stuck in a strange time warp and while running look like they are doing their best impressions to avoid conflict altogether. They are slow, cumbersome and awkward yet they can leap through the air with all the grace and agility of a cat. Very peculiar.

You can switch between partner characters to solve puzzles and each come loaded with their own inventory and play style, complete with a basic crafting system that allows the player to juryrig their own survival tools out of certain objects found throughout the world, such as molotovs, explosive bombs or herb combinations, with it only being the first episode, this may grow over time as I also found gunpowder, hinting at a more robust crafting system to come as the episodes are released. Claire will use sheer firepower and brute force to smash through resistance you find along the way whilst Moira opts to wield only a flashlight and crowbar which comes with its own game mechanics, she can blind enemies with her flashlight and follow up with a devestating strike from her crowbar, guns are out for her by pacifists choice, but give her an item she can do blunt force trauma with; wind her up and watch her go (makes sense right?). The controls are really what you would expect, they are digital, best with controller and appropriately tanky, but you wont find yourself hard up for maneuvering and traversing the environment nor is there any grievances with aiming. For the most part though this all feels believeably justified with each characters background story and offers a unique and indepth combat system which offers itself well to cooperative play which brings me to our highlight.

CAPCOM use to be such an upstanding company with a wide diverse catalog of games that while not all award winners were, in fact, rather fun and varied. RER2 EP 1 plays absolutely horrendously. The cons outweigh the pros thus far in this disastrous addition to the RE series and not even the absolute nostalgic novelty of playing Barry Burton can or ever could take the sting of betrayal, shady business practices, and simply bad ports that CAPCOM continues to employ when it comes to their offerings to the PC market.

Now there is no mistake about it I am a massive Resident Evil fan and rank some of the earlier titles as my favourite games of all time. Unfortunately some of the more recent titles have lost a little bit of what made the earlier games special. The original Resident Evil Revelations changed this when it was released on 3DS a few years ago. 

Set on an abandoned ship it provided an experience much more akin to what made the original games in the series so good.

Needless to say I rank Revelations as one of my favourite games of all time and was very excited when I heard they were making a sequal. Now unlike the previous this game is made in episodes that are each being released one week apart to make the whole game. Normally I am not a fan of episodes as they come miles apart and I lose interest but the fact they are 1 week apart and the “Next time on Revelations 2” that is presented to you upon completion of the first episode really dragged me in to its world.

Episode 1: Penal Colony see Resident Evil Alumni Claire Redfield and Barry Burton’s daughter Moira Burton taken by a military group and imprisoned apparently as test subjects in a SAW like game. You play as these character trying to escape and find help. The second half of the game sees you playa s Barry Burton trying to rescue his daughter along with Natalia a young child he meets upon arrival who seemingly has some kind of abnormal powers. The pairing of these 2 is very akin to the relationship between Joel and Ellie in The Last of Us. 

These pairings work well and as a solo player the switching between the characters is handled perfectly with little mess. There were a few times when evading monsters the ai character seemed determined to hump the thing we were running away from’s leg but generally this was a small thing. Now there has been some controversy recently that the Steam version does not support local co-op but the PS4 and XB1 versions do. Personally I am not overly fussed by this but if this is something that will factor into your decision to buy this game please bear it in mind. 

The relationship between the characters in excellent and unlike normal Resident Evil games the voice acting is pretty decent. A personal favourite of mine sees Barry making a quick remark about “Now whose the master of unpicking locks” right after using a crane to destroy a door.

Gameplay wise this builds well on the previous game but as this time it was not designed for DS it controls a lot better. I played with a 360 pad but equally my short time playing with a mouse and keyboard seemed pretty good to. 
Graphically the game is a mixed bag. Visually pretty decent but the locations themselves while atmospheric are rather dull and could have done with a little more intrigue… but this is Resident Evil after all. 

The raid mode again a decent diversions once you have finished the main game but this section allows the creep of one of the game’s biggest annoyances… micro transactions. 

There is no need to have this in a single player game but you can use it to buy weapons and health and hearts for use in RAID mode which is totally unnecessary and leave a bit of a sour taste. Coupled with the local co-op that was removed from advertised on the steam release right before sale and Capcom aren’t trying to win any PR competitions.

But overall I must say I really enjoyed episode 1 of Resident Evil Revelations 2. Its well made its engaging and I cannot wait to tune in to episode 2 next week.

This game has so much potential, it’s a shame to see that Capcom has ruined the PC port.  First the objective stuff, then the personal complains:

[OBJECTIVE] = First off, the main story mode is basically unplayable.  The game lags constantly, often just straight-up freezing when there are more than two people on screen (which, since you are always with an AI companion, is anytime there is a single enemy on screen).  I have fiddled with the settings more than I care to discuss, and nothing works.  Looking online, some people suggest locking the fps, others suggest unlocking it, some suggest turning v-sync off, some suggest turning it on; basically, no one has any idea how to fix this mess.  I’m not going to go into a long, detailed description of my specs, but suffice it to say that I can run games with much larger environments, more effects, better graphics, and better, well, EVERYTHING without any issues.  I was able to get raid mode to work, but even then it jittered here and there.

Also, the camera is “sticky”; when you move the camera while aiming it lags for a second (just the reticule, not the whole game) and then zips up to its proper speed.  As I’m sure you can imagine, this makes getting head shots, or, rather, ANY type of shot very difficult and frustrating.

Based on all the other reviews, I know I am not the only one having these issues.  I would not recommend getting this game until people start to say that they are fixed.

[PERSONAL] = There are just so many design choices that make no sense.  First of all, why are custom parts locked to guns in raid mode?  Half the fun in RE Revelations was experimenting to see what was optimal.  Who cares if there are tons more custom parts now; no one is going to risk wasting time and money on a new, totally-strange gun load out if you have to destroy the gun to get the parts back or destroy the parts to get the gun back.  It’s supposed to make you really consider whether you want to put parts onto a gun, but everyone is just going to go with the tried-and-true parts like increased damage or increased magazine size and then destroy the gun to roll those parts over to a new gun of the same type when they get one.

And then there is Moira Burton, the workshopped-to-death punk girl wannabe who is constantly freaking out about all the blood and gore and violence around her.  Now, yes, it is reasonable that a girl of her age and background would act this way but that does not make it any less annoying.  This is RESIDENT EVIL; blood and gore are as common as bad dialog here.

She also has this weird thing with guns in that she won’t use them or even acknowledge them, really.  When you get your first gun, right after the two of you were nearly killed by an enemy (who then went on to brutally murder another girl in front of you two, more on her in a second) she asks, “are you going to use that?”  No, Moira, I’m going to stick it in my butt so I can play Russian roulette every time I sit down.

Yes, yes, her aversion to guns is supposed to allude to some tragic event in her past but WE ARE IN A SURVIVAL SITUATION, MOIRA.  It's bad enough that I have to switch to you to find hidden items and kill stunned enemies, but can you at least harden up and stop talking to me?

Last, and certainly not least in my list of petty complaints: do you remembers Rachel Foley, the super-hot blonde combat specialist from RE Revelations?  Did you like having her in raid mode?  You did?  Well, good news!  RE Revelations 2 has her ugly, brown-haired, glasses-wearing, office-nerd sister!  Isn’t that just GREAT?!

Now, I would like to note that I am posting this on Feb. 25th, the day of release of the first episode on steam.  Once all of the episodic content is out the lag issues, stickiness issues, and the lack of Rachel Foley might be fixed (since they are releasing more raid mode characters with each episode); if they are then please disregard those complaints.

That being said, Capcom still chose to release this game with all of the lag and stickiness.  It just goes to show why you should never, ever pre-order a game even if it is from a company you respect and trust.  I don’t think this will be my last Capcom game, but it will certainly be the last game that I ever pre-order.
